x: We have explained the meaning of God Almighty’s statement, Alif, Lam, Meem, and we have mentioned the statements of the people of interpretation regarding its interpretation, which is more correct than their statements in our view, with its evidence in what has passed, so there is no need to repeat it in this place.
The translators of the Qur’an differed in their interpretation of the words of God Almighty: Alif, Lam, Meem.
Some of them said: It is one of the names of the Qur’an.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Alif, Lam, Meem, he said: It is one of the names of the Qur’an.

c: Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim Al-Amili told me: Abu Hudhayfah Musa bin Masʿud told us: Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Alif, Lam, Meem is one of the names of the Qur’an.

c: Al-Qasim bin Al-Hasan told us: Al-Hussein bin Dawud told us: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: Alif, Lam, Meem is one of the names of the Qur’an.

x: Some of them said: They are opening verses with which God opens the Quran.
Those who said this were:

c: Harun ibn Idris al-Asamm al-Kufi told me: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Maharbi told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Alif, Lam, Meem are opening verses with which God opens the Qur’an.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim Al-Ghafari told us: Abu Naim told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Alif, Lam, Meem are opening letters.

c: Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim told me: Ishaq bin Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Adam, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Alif, Lam, Meem, Alif, Muḥammad, and Sad are the opening letters with which God began.

c: Al-Qasim bin Al-Hasan told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: like the hadith of Harun bin Idris.

x: Others said: It is the name of the Surah.
Those who said this are:

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said: Abdullah bin Wahb told us, he said:
m: I asked Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam about the words of God: “Alif, Lam, Meem. This is the Book,” and “Alif, Lam, Meem. This is a revelation,” and “Alif, Lam, Meem. That is the name of the chapters.” He said: My father said: They are only the names of the chapters.

x: Some of them said: It is the greatest name of God.
Those who said this are:

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us: Shu’bah told us:
m: I asked al-Suddi about Ha Meem, “Ta Seen Meem,” and Alif Lam Meem. He said: Ibn Abbas said: They are the greatest name of God.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Abu al-Nu’man told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ismail al-Suddi, on the authority of Murrah al-Hamadani, who said: Abdullah said:
m: He mentioned something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Ishaq bin Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Musa, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: The openings of the surahs are among the names of God.

x: Some of them said: It is an oath by which God swears, and it is one of His names.
Those who said this were:

c: Yahya bin Othman bin Saleh Al-Sahmi told me, he said: Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: It is an oath by which God swears, and it is one of the names of God.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Khalid Al-Hadha’ told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: Alif, Lam, Meem is an oath.

x: Some of them said: It is a collection of letters separated from nouns and verbs, each letter having a meaning different from the meaning of the other letter.
Those who said this are:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Wakiʿ told us, and Sufyan ibn Wakiʿ told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ataʿ ibn al-Saʿib, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Alif, Lam, Meem. He said: I, God, know best.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Abu Ubaid,
m: who said: Abu Al-Yaqzan narrated to us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, who said: His statement, Alif, Lam, Meem, he said: I, God, know best.

c: Musa bin Harun Al-Hamdani told me: Amr bin Hammad Al-Qannad told us: Asbat bin Nasr told us, on the authority of Ismail Al-Suddi in a report he mentioned, on the authority of Abu Malik, and on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and on the authority of Murrah Al-Hamdani, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, and on the authority of some of the companions of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace: Alif, Lam, Meem. He said: As for Alif, Lam, Meem, it is a letter derived from the letters of the spelling of the names of God, may His praise be exalted.
b.via: some of the companions of the Prophet

c: Muhammad ibn Muammar told us: Abbas ibn Ziyad al-Bahili told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement: Alif, Lam, Meem, “Ha, Meem,” and Nun, he said: It is a disconnected noun.

x: Some of them said that they are letters of the alphabet that were placed.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: It was narrated on the authority of Mansur ibn Abi Nuwayrah,
m: who said: Abu Saeed al-Mu'addab narrated to us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The opening letters of all the surahs, Qaf, "Sad, Ha Meem, Ta Seen Meem, Alif Lam Ra," and others, are a fabricated spelling.

x: Some of them said: They are letters, each of which includes various different meanings.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim Al-Tabari told me: Ishaq bin Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar Al-Razi, who said: My father told me, on the authority of Al-Rabi bin Anas,
m: regarding the statement of God, the Most High: Alif, Lam, Meem, he said: These letters, from the twenty-nine letters, are spoken by all tongues. There is not a letter among them that is not a key to one of His names. There is not a letter among them that is not related to His favors and trials, and there is not a letter among them that is not related to the duration of a people and their appointed times. Jesus, son of Mary, said: And it is strange that they speak of His names and live in His provision, so how can they deny Him? He said: The Alif is the key to His name: God, the Lam is the key to His name: Latif, and the Mim is the key to His name: Majeed. The Alif is the favors of God, the Lam is His kindness, and the Mim is His glory. The Alif is years, the Lam is thirty years, and the Mim is forty years.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: something similar.

x: Some of them said: These are letters from the abjad numeral system. We were reluctant to mention the one who narrated this, as the one who narrated it was someone whose narration and transmission were not reliable. A similar narration has already been reported from Al-Rabi' ibn Anas.
Some of them said: Every book has a secret, and the secret of the Qur’an is its openings. As for the Arabists, they differed about the meaning of that.

Some of them said: They are letters from the alphabetical letters, and mentioning what was mentioned of them at the beginnings of the surahs dispensed with mentioning the rest of them, which are the completion of the twenty-eight letters, just as the informant dispensed with mentioning what he reported that there are twenty-eight letters in the alphabet by mentioning A B T Th, without mentioning the rest of its letters, which are the completion of the twenty-eight. He said: Therefore, that book was raised, because the meaning of the speech is: Alif, Lam, and Mim are from the separate letters, that is the book which I have revealed to you all together, there is no doubt about it.
A B T Th has become like a noun in the letters of the alphabet, just as Al-Hamd was the name of the Opening of the Book.

Since it was permissible for a speaker to say: My son is in Ṭā Ḍaḥ, and it was known from his saying that if he said it that he wanted to report about his son that he was in the disconnected letters, it was known from that that Ṭā Ḍaḥdoes not have a name, even if that was more effective in mentioning than the rest of them.

He said: The difference between mentioning the letters of the alphabet in the openings of the surahs is that they are mentioned at their beginnings differently, and they are mentioned when they are mentioned at their beginnings, which are A B T Th, together, in order to separate the report about them if what is meant by mentioning what is mentioned from them differently is to indicate connected speech and if what is meant by mentioning what is mentioned from them together is to indicate the separate letters specifically. And they cited as evidence for the permissibility of the saying of the speaker: My son in T Z and the like, from the report about it that it is in the letters of the alphabet, and that this is from his saying in the statement that it takes the place of his saying: My son in A B T Th in the rajaz of some of the rajaz poets of Banu Asad: Surat Spider: 1
h
When I saw her matter in Hatti

and I joked about her lying and flattery I took from her the horns of the Shamat, and she has not left me with her and her giving Even the head was covered with blood He claimed that he meant by that the report about the woman that she was in Abu Jad, so he made his statement:
h
When I saw her matter in Hatti
, in place of his report about her that she was in Abu Jad, since that was from his statement, indicating to his listener what his statement: When I saw her matter in Abu Jad indicates to him.

Others said: Rather, it was started with this at the beginning of the surahs to open the ears of the polytheists to listening to it, as they had advised each other to turn away from the Qur’an, so that when they listened to it, the composition of it would be recited to them.
Some of them said: The letters that open the Surahs are letters with which God opens His speech.
Is there anything in the Qur’an that has no meaning?
The meaning of this is that he began with it to indicate that the surah before it had ended, and that he had begun another, so he made this a sign of the break between them.

This is in the speech of the Arabs, when a man among them recites poetry and says: But, a town whose people are not human He says: No, it did not stir up sorrows and grief But it is not from the verse and is not counted in its meter, but it is used to interrupt a sentence and start another.

Each of the statements made by those whose statement we have described in this regard has a known basis. As for those who said: Alif, Lam, Meem is one of the names of the Qur’an, there are two aspects to their statement: One: That they meant that "Alif, Lam, Meem is the name of the Qur'an, just as Al-Furqan" is its name. If the meaning of the speaker is thus, then the interpretation of his statement, "Alif, Lam, Meem. This is the Book," is to mean an oath. It is as if he said: By the Qur'an, this Book, there is no doubt about it. The other of them: That they meant that it is one of the names of the surah by which it is known, just as all other things are known by their names which have signs by which they are known. So the listener understands from the speaker saying: Today I read Al-Muddaththir and Al-Nun, meaning the surahs that he read from the surahs of the Qur’an, just as he understands from him if he says: Today I met Amr and Zayd, and they know by Zayd and Amr what he met from the people.

If the meaning of this is unclear to someone, he may say: How can this be so, when there are a number of surahs similar to alif, lam, meem and alif, lam-ra in the Qur’an? Names are only indicators if they distinguish between people, but if they are not distinguishing, then they are not indicators. It has been said: Although the names have become, due to the commonality of many people in one of them, not distinctive except by other meanings with it, such as adding the relation of the named to it, or its description or attribute, in a way that distinguishes it from other forms of it, they were initially established for distinction, no doubt. Then, when there is a need for the meanings that distinguish between those named by them. Likewise, in the names of the surahs, each name, according to the one who said this, was made an indication of the surah named by it. So, since the named shares in it other surahs of the Qur’an, the one reporting a surah from it needed to add to its name the named by it something that would differentiate the hearer between reporting about it and others, of a description, attribute, or other than that.

So the one reporting about himself says that he recited Surat Al-Baqarah, if he calls it by its name, which is Alif, Lam, Meem: I read Alif, Lam, Meem, Al-Baqarah. And in Al Imran 3:I read Alif, Lam, Meem, Al Imran. And “Alif, Lam, Meem. That is the Book.” "And "And, 'Alif, Lam, Mim. God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining." It is as if he wanted to inform about two men, each of whose name was Amr, except that one of them was Tamimi and the other Azdi, he would have to say to the one he wanted to inform about them: I met Amr al-Tamimi and Amr al-Azdi, since there is no difference between them and others who share their names, except their lineage. This is also the case with those who interpret the disconnected letters as names of surahs. As for those who said: These are openings with which God Almighty begins His speech, they directed that to something similar to the meaning we narrated from the one we narrated that from among the Arabs, that he said: These are evidence of the end of a surah and the beginning of another, and a sign of the interruption of what is between them, just as you made rather at the beginning of a poem an indication of the beginning of it and the end of another before it.

Just as we mentioned about the Arabs, when they wanted to begin reciting a poem, they would say: Rather, what stirred up sorrows and grief had been grief. But it is not from the house nor is it included in its meter, but it is used to indicate the end of one speech and the beginning of another.

These are disconnected letters, some of which are names of God Almighty, and some of which are attributes of Him, and each letter has a meaning other than the meaning of the other letter, then they interpreted this in a manner similar to the poet’s saying: We said to her: Stand for us. She said: Stand. Don't think that we forgot to stand.

Meaning by his saying: Qalata Qaf, she said: I have stopped. So by making the Qaf pronounced from Waqafa, she indicated what she meant by the completion of the word in which she stopped. So they diverted his saying Alif, Lam, Meem and the like to something like this meaning.

Some of them said: The Alif is the Alif of Ana, the Lam is the Lam of God, and the Meem is the Meem of A’lam, and each letter of them indicates a complete word. They said: So the sum of these disconnected letters, if they appear with each letter of them, completes the letters of the word, Ana, God A’lam. They said: And likewise all that is at the beginning of the chapters of the Qur’an from that, so based on this meaning and this interpretation, they said: It is widespread and apparent in the speech of the Arabs that the speaker among them reduces letters from the word, if what remains indicates what was deleted from it and adds to it what is not from it, if the addition does not confuse its meaning to its listener, like their deletion in the reduction of the Tha’ from Harith, so they say Ya Har, and from Malik the Kaf, so they say Ya Mal, and the like, and like the saying of their rajaz poet: What is wrong with the oppressed?

How can he not save his skin if he does not? As if he wanted to say: If he does such and such, he was satisfied with the letter ya from yaf’ala, and as another of them said: Good things come to you, and evil things come to you. He wants: evil. I don't want evil unless you He wants: unless you wish, so he was satisfied with the ta’ and the fa’ in both words, from the rest of their letters, and other similar examples that would take too long to cover in the book.

c: And as Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub and Ibn Awn, on the authority of Muhammad, he said:
m: When Yazid bin Muawiyah died, Abda said to me: I do not see it except as a trial, so flee from your estate and join your family. I said: What do you command me? He said: I would prefer for you to... Ayoub and Ibn Awn said, with his hand under his right cheek, describing lying down until you see a matter that you recognize.

x: He meant by Ṭadtajiʿu, so he sufficed with the Ṭadtajiʿu from Ṭadtajiʿu. And as the other said in the addition to the statement, in the manner that I described: I say, when you fell on the hump, O my camel, you have not traveled far He wants: all of it, and as the other said: My shape and your shape are different, so stick to the short ones and lower your whites So he added a letter Ḍād, but it is not in the word. They said: Likewise, what is missing from the complete letters of each of these words that we mentioned is the completion of the letters Alif-Lam-Meem and its counterparts is similar to what is missing from the speech that we narrated from the Arabs in their poetry and speech. As for those who said: Every letter of alif-laam-meem and its counterparts indicates various meanings, like what we mentioned from Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas, they explained that to the same interpretation as he explained to him who said: It is based on the interpretation God knows best, in that every letter of it is some of the letters of a complete word, and its indication of its completeness suffices without mentioning its completeness, even though they disagreed with him regarding every letter of that: Is it from the word that the proponents of the first opinion claimed it was from, or from another one?

They said: Rather, the alif of alif-laam-meem is from various words, and it indicates the meanings of all of that and its completeness. They said: Each letter of that was isolated, and was limited by it to completing the letters of the word, because if all of the letters of the word were made clear, the word that is made clear, in which some of these disconnected letters are some, would only indicate one meaning, not two meanings or more than that. They said: Since there is no indication in that, if all of them were made clear, except for their meaning, which is a single meaning, and since God, the Most High, intended to indicate with each letter many meanings for one thing, it is not permissible except to isolate the letter indicating those meanings, so that those addressed by it know that God, the Mighty and Sublime, did not intend to intend one meaning and indicate one thing with what He addressed them with, and that He only intended to indicate many things with it.

They said: The Alif in Alif, Lam, Meem implies many meanings, including the completion of the name of the Lord, which is God, and the completion of the name of God’s blessings, which are His favors, and the indication that the lifespan of a people is one year, since the Alif in the abjad system is one. The Lam implies the completion of the name of God, which is Latif, and the completion of the name of His bounty, which is Lutf, and the indication that the lifespan of a people is thirty years. The Mim implies the completion of the name of God, which is Majestic, and the completion of the name of His Greatness, which is Majestic, and the indication that the lifespan of a people is forty years. The meaning of the speech, according to the interpretation of those who say the first opinion, is that God, may He be glorified and exalted, began His speech by describing Himself as the All-Knowing from whom nothing is hidden, and He made that a method for His servants to follow at the beginning of their sermons, letters, and affairs, and a test from Him for them so that they may deserve a great reward in the abode of recompense, just as He began with Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, and Praise be to God, who created the heavens and the earth (al-An’am 6:1), and other similar surahs whose openings He made praise of Himself, and just as He made the openings of some of them glorifying and venerating Himself with praise, as He, may He be glorified and exalted, said: Glory be to Him who took His servant by night (al-Isra’ 17:1), and other similar surahs of the Qur’an, the openings of some of which He made praising Himself, the openings of some of Surat Spider: 1 which glorifying Him, and the openings of some of which glorifying and sanctifying Him.

Likewise, He made the keys to the other surahs, which begin with some letters of the alphabet, praises of Himself, sometimes with knowledge, sometimes with justice and fairness, and sometimes with generosity and kindness, in brief and concise terms, then the matters are summarized after that. According to this interpretation, the alif, lam, and mim in the places of the nominative case should be raised by each other, without his saying that book, and that book would be a predicate subject separate from the meaning of alif, lam, mim. Likewise, that in the interpretation of the statement of the one who says this second statement, is raised by each other, even if its meaning is different from the meaning of the statement of the one who says the first statement. As for those who said: They are letters from the letters of the abjad calculation without any meanings that contradict that, they said: We do not know of any meaning for the disconnected letters that can be understood other than the abjad calculation, and other than the spelling of the saying of the speaker: Alif, Lam, Meem.

They said: It is not permissible for God, the Most High, to address His servants except in a way that they understand and comprehend. Since that is the case and His saying Alif, Lam, Meem does not have a rational face that could be directed to it, except one of the two faces that we mentioned, then one of its faces is invalidated, which is that it is intended by it to spell Alif, Lam, Meem. It is correct and proven that it is intended by it to mean the second face, which is the abjad calculation, because the saying of the speaker: Alif, Lam, Meem cannot be followed by the statement That is the Book, because the meaning of the statement is impossible and goes beyond reason, if “Alif, Lam, Meem. That is the Book” follows it.
They also argued for their statement with the following:

c: Muhammad ibn Humayd al-Razi narrated to us: Salamah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me: al-Kalbi narrated to me, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah ibn Ri’ab, who said:
m: “Abu Yasir ibn Akhtab passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was reciting the opening verse of Surat al-Baqarah 2:‘Alif, Lam, Meem. This is the Book about which there is no doubt.’ So his brother Huyayy ibn Akhtab from the Jews came and said: ‘By God, you know that I heard Muhammad reciting, in what God, the Almighty, revealed to him, ‘Alif, Lam, Meem. This is the Book.’ They said: Did you hear it? He said: ‘Yes!’ So Huyayy ibn Akhtab walked with those Jews to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: ‘O Muhammad, was it not mentioned to us that you recite, in what was revealed to you, ‘Alif, Lam, Meem. This is the Book.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Yes.’ They said: ‘Did Gabriel bring this to you from God?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ They said: God, the Almighty, has sent prophets before you, and we do not know of any prophet among them who explained what…’” His reign was prolonged and his nation did not eat except you! So Huyayy ibn Akhtab said, and he turned to those who were with him and said to them: The Alif is one, the Lam is thirty, and the Mim is forty, so that is seventy-one years. Will you enter the religion of a prophet whose reign and nation did not eat except for seventy-one years? He said: Then he turned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, is there anything else with this? He said: Yes. He said: What? He said: Alif-Lam-Meem. He said: This is heavier and longer. The Alif is one, the Lam is thirty, the Mim is forty, and the Sad is ninety, so that is one hundred and sixty-one years. Is there anything else with this, O Muhammad? He said: Yes. He said: What? He said: Alif-Lam-Ra. He said: By God, this is heavier and longer. The Alif is one, the Lam is thirty, and the Ra is two hundred, so that is two hundred and thirty-one years. He said: Is there anything else with this, O Muhammad? He said: Yes, al-murr. He said: By God, this is heavier and longer. The alif is one, the lam is thirty, the mim is forty, and the ra is two hundred. This is two hundred and seventy-one years. Then he said: Your matter has become so confusing to us, O Muhammad, that we do not know whether you have been given a little or a lot. Then they got up from him. Abu Yasir said to his brother Huyayy ibn Akhtab and the rabbis who were with him: How do you know? Perhaps he has gathered all of this for Muhammad: seventy-one, sixty-one and one hundred, two hundred and thirty-one, two hundred and seventy-one. That is seven hundred and thirty-four years! They said: His matter has become confusing to us! They claim that these verses were revealed about them: “It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book. In it are verses that are precise - they are the foundation of the Book - and others unspecific.”
r
(Al Imran 3:7)

They said: This report clearly proves the correctness of what we have said about this interpretation, and the corruption of what our opponents have said about it. The correct statement in my opinion about the interpretation of the keys to the Surahs, which are the letters of the alphabet, is that God, the Most High, made them separate letters and did not connect some of them to others, making them like all other speech with connected letters, because He, the Most High, intended by His wording to indicate with each letter many meanings, not just one meaning, as Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said. Even though Ar-Rabi’ limited it to three meanings, without anything more than that. The correct interpretation of this, in my opinion, is that each letter of it contains what Al-Rabi’ said, and what all other commentators have said about it, except for what I mentioned from the people of Arabic who I mentioned: that he directed the interpretation of this to that they are letters of the alphabet. Mentioning what he mentioned of it in the keys to the surahs suffices, without mentioning the rest of the twenty-eight letters of the alphabet, by interpreting: that these letters, that book, are collected, there is no doubt about it, for it is a false and corrupt statement, as it departs from the statements of all the companions and followers and those who came after them from the dissenters of the people of interpretation and exegesis. So it is sufficient to indicate his error, the testimony of the proof against him of the error, with the invalidation of the one who said that, as we have narrated from him, when he turned to explaining the raising of that book by saying once that each one of them is raised by its companion, and another time that it is raised by the referent of what he mentioned in his saying there is no doubt about it, and once by his saying a guidance for the righteous. This is an omission from him, based on his statement that alif, lam, mim is the subject of that book, and a departure from the statement he claimed in the interpretation of “alif, lam, mim. That book,” and that the interpretation of that is: these letters are that book.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: How can one letter be comprehensive in indicating many different meanings?

Just as it is possible for a single word to include many different meanings, such as their saying for a group of al-Nas 114:a nation, and for a particular moment in time: a nation, and for a devout and obedient man: a nation, and for religion and creed: a groan. And like their saying for recompense and retaliation: a religion, and for authority and obedience: a religion, and for humiliation: a religion, and for accountability: a religion, and there are many similar things that would take a long time to list, as speech is made with one word, and it includes many meanings. And likewise the statement of God, may He be praised: Alif, Lam, Meem, “Alif, Lam, Ra,” Alif, Lam, Meem, and what is similar to that from the letters of the alphabet which are the opening letters of the surahs, each letter of which denotes various meanings, encompassing all of them from the names and attributes of God, the Almighty, as the commentators have said from the sayings we have mentioned. And they are, however, the opening letters of the surahs, as those who have said so have said. And the fact that these are from the letters of the names and attributes of God, may He be praised, does not prevent them from being opening letters for the surahs.

Because God, may He be glorified and praised, has opened many chapters of the Qur’an with praise and thanks to Himself, and many of them with glorification and exaltation of Him, so it is not impossible that some of them begin with an oath by Him. As for the ones whose opening letters begin with the letters of the alphabet, one of the meanings of their opening letters is that they are the opening letters of the chapters of the Qur’an. They are among what God swore by, because one of their meanings is that they are letters of the names and attributes of God, the Most High, as we have explained previously. There is no doubt that the meaning of swearing by God, His names and attributes is correct. They are among the letters of the abjad system. They are symbols and names for the chapters that begin with them. This encompasses the meanings of all that we have described, from what we have explained, from its aspects.

Because if God, the Most High, had intended by this, or part of it, to indicate a single meaning from what it could bear, without all other meanings, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would have made that clear to them. This is because God, the Most High, only revealed His Book to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to clarify to them what they differed about. And in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, not explaining that, that some of its interpretations are intended by it and not others, is the clearest evidence that it is intended by all of its aspects for which it is possible. It was not impossible in the mind for any of them to be from its interpretation and meaning, just as it was not impossible for the many meanings of one word to come together, in one expression, in one statement. Whoever rejects what we have said about this should be asked about the difference between this and other letters that have a single pronunciation, yet contain many different meanings, such as nation, religion, and similar nouns and verbs.

He will not say anything about one of these without necessarily saying the same thing about the other. Likewise, anyone who interprets any of these things in a way that is different from the other ways we have described should be asked about the proof for his claim, from the way that must be accepted. Then he should counter with the statement of his opponent on this matter, and ask about the difference between them: from the origin, or from what the origin indicates. So he will not say one statement without requiring the same in the other.

i: As for the grammarians who claimed that this is similar to the saying of the poet:
x: Rather, what stirred up sorrows and grief had been grief.

And that it has no meaning, but rather it is an addition to the speech whose meaning is to throw it away, so he made a mistake in many ways: One of them is that he described God Almighty as having addressed the Arabs in a language other than their own, nor in the language of any human being. Although the Arabs used to begin their poetry with bal, it is known that they never began any of their speech with alif, lam, meem, “alif, ra,” or alif, mas, in the sense of beginning it with bal. And since that was not part of their beginning, and God Almighty only addressed them with what He addressed them from the Qur’an, with what they knew of their languages and what they used among themselves of their speech, in every verse, then there is no doubt that the path of what we have described of the letters of the alphabet, with which the beginnings of the surahs, which are openings, is the path of the rest of the Qur’an, in that He did not deviate with them from the languages they knew and used among themselves in their speech.

Because if this was deviated from the path of their languages and logic, it would be outside the meaning of clarification with which God, the Almighty, described the Qur’an, when He, the Most High, said:
The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart, that you may be among the warners, in a clear Arabic tongue

How can something be made clear that no one in the world can comprehend or understand, according to the statement of the one who said this statement, and that is not known in the language of any of the created beings, according to his statement? And in God’s statement that it is a clear Arabic, there is what belies this statement, and indicates that the Arabs were knowledgeable about it, and it is clear to them. This is Surat Spider: 1 one of the aspects of his error. The second aspect of his error in this regard is that by attributing it to God, the Most High, He addressed His servants with something that has no benefit or meaning for them, through speech in which it is the same to address them with it or not to address them with it.

This is by attributing the futility that is denied in the words of all monotheists about God to God, the Most High. The third aspect of his error is that bal in the speech of the Arabs has an interpretation and meaning, and that they include it in their speech to return to a statement that has already been completed, like their saying: It was not your brother who came to me, but rather your father, and I did not see Omar, but rather Abdullah, and similar statements, as A’sha of Banu Tha’labah said: And I will drink eight, eight, thirteen, two, and four. He continued his speech until he said: In the sitting, and the goodness of his arms is like a balloon that hits me like a finger Then he said: Rather, count this, in another verse, and mention a young man of generous nature, the most wonderful. It is as if he said: Leave this and take up another style of poetry. Rather, it only comes in the speech of the Arabs in this manner of speech.

As for opening their speech with a beginning meaning of length and deletion, without indicating a meaning, that is something that we do not know of anyone who has claimed from the people of knowledge of the Arabic language and its logic, except for the one whose statement you mentioned. So that would be a principle by which the letters of the dictionary, which are the openings of the chapters of the Qur’an that were opened with it, could be likened if they were similar to it, so how is it that it is far from resembling it?

evidence.text: Others said: Rather, it was started with this at the beginning of the surahs to open the ears of the polytheists to listening to it, as they had advised each other to turn away from the Qur’an, so that when they listened to it, the composition of it would be recited to them.

x: As for his statement:
h
Do people think that they will be left alone to say
, ‘We believe,’
h
and they will not be tested

? its meaning is: I think that those of your companions who left, O Muhammad, because of the harm the polytheists did to them, will be left alone without being tested or tried, because they said, We believe in you, O Muhammad, and we believe you in what you brought us from God. No, but that We may test them, so that the truthful among them may be distinguished from the liar. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, We believe,
h
and they will not be tested
, he said: They will be tested in their persons and their wealth.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And they will not be tested
means they will not be afflicted.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hashim, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they will not be tested

, he said: They will not be tested. The first is in the accusative case according to hasaba, and the second is in the accusative case according to some Arab scholars, because they are left behind and not informed of it. The meaning of the statement, according to his saying,
h
Do people think that they will be left behind is because they say

, We believe. So when the lam of the preposition was deleted from for, it was in the accusative case as I mentioned. As for the saying of others, it is in the accusative case due to the omission of the preposition. The Arabs hardly ever say, I left someone behind without introducing an into the statement. Rather, they say, I left him behind. And an was introduced here because the statement was sufficient with his saying, that they will be left behind, since its meaning was: Do people think that they will be left behind
h
and they will not be tested

, in order for them to say, We believe? So his saying, that they will be left behind was sufficient for it to be applied to the people, not to their report. And if you had made an in his saying, that they say in the accusative case with the intention of repeating I think, it would have been permissible, and the meaning of the statement would be: Do people think that they will be left behind? They think that they will say, We believe,
h
and they will not be tested

x: God Almighty says: And We have certainly tested those before them of the nations, to whom We sent Our messengers, and they said the same as your nation said, O Muhammad, with their enemies, and Our enabling them to harm them, like Moses when We sent him to the Prophet of Israel, so We tested them with Pharaoh and his chiefs, and like Jesus when We sent him to the Children of Israel, so We tested those who followed him with those who turned away from him. Thus, We have tested your followers with those who oppose you from among your enemies. So God will surely make evident those of them who are truthful in their saying, We believe, “and He will surely make evident those of them who are liars” in their saying, and God knows that about them before the test, during the test, and after the test. But the meaning of that is: And God will make evident the truthfulness of the truthful among them in his saying, We believe in God, from the falsity of the liar among them by testing him with his enemy, so that He will make evident his truthfulness from his falsity, his allies, in the manner that we have explained previously.
He mentioned that this verse was revealed about a group of Muslims who were tortured by the polytheists.
Some of them were tempted, and some of them were patient with their harm until God brought them relief from Him.
The narration mentioned that:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: I heard Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair say: This verse was revealed, meaning: “Alif, Lam, Meem. Do people think that they will be left to say, ‘We believe’”… to His saying:
h
And that He will make known the liars
, about Ammar bin Yasir, when he was being tortured for the sake of God.

x: Others said: Rather, this was revealed for the sake of a people who had declared Islam in Mecca, but had not emigrated. The trial that befell these people, based on the statement of these people, was the emigration by which they were tested.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Matar, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: It was revealed, meaning “Alif, Lam, Meem. Do people think that they will be abandoned” the two verses about people who were in Mecca and had acknowledged Islam. The companions of Muhammad, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to them from Medina: No acknowledgement of Islam will be accepted from you until you emigrate. So they went out intending to go to Medina, and the polytheists pursued them and turned them back. So this verse was revealed about them. So they wrote to them: Such and such a verse has been revealed about you. They said: We will go out, and if anyone follows us, we will fight him. So they went out, and the polytheists pursued them and fought them. Then some of them were killed and some of them were saved. So God revealed about them: “Then indeed, your Lord is to those who emigrated after they were persecuted and then strove and were patient. Indeed, your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful.” (al-Nahl 16:110) Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said:

c: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And We have certainly tried he said: We have been tested.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hashim, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: And We certainly tried those before them, he said: We tested those before them.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Hashim, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And We certainly tried those before them means We tested them

x: God Almighty says: Or do those who associate others with God and worship others besides Him think that they will outstrip Us? They are the ones meant by His statement:
h
Those who do evil deeds think that they will outstrip Us

. He says: That they will outsmart Us and make themselves lost to Us, so that We will not be able to defeat them and take revenge on them for associating others with God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
Or do those who do evil deeds think meaning polytheism that they will outstrip us

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, that they should outstrip us means that they should outsmart us. And His statement:
h
Evil is their judgment
. God Almighty says:
h
Evil is their judgment
that they judge that these people who commit evil deeds will precede us with their own souls.

x: God Almighty says: Whoever hopes for the Day of Meeting with God and desires His reward, then the appointed time that God has set for the resurrection of His creation for recompense and punishment will come soon, and He is the All-Hearing. He says: And God is He whom this hopeful hopes for His reward when he meets Him, the All-Hearing of his words: We believe in God, the All-Knowing of the truth of his words, that he has believed in his lie concerning it.
And His statement:
h
And whoever strives
, strives only for himself, meaning:
h
And whoever strives

against his enemy from among the polytheists, strives only for himself, because he does that seeking reward from God for his striving, and escaping punishment. So God has no need for his doing that, and that is because God is independent of all of His creation. His is the kingdom, creation, and command.

God Almighty says: And those who believed in God and His Messenger, and their faith was sound when God tested them and tried them, and they did not turn away from their religions because of the harm the polytheists did to them, and did righteous deeds - We will surely remove from them their misdeeds that they had committed in their polytheism, and We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do meaning: And We will reward them for their righteous deeds in their Islam, the best of what they used to do when they were polytheists, along with Our removing their evil deeds.

God Almighty says, And We have enjoined upon man, in what We revealed to Our Messenger, “concerning his parents that he should treat them goodly. The Arab scholars differed on the reason for the accusative case of al-Hasan. Some Basran grammarians said: It is accusative with the intention of repeating the word ‘wassana’ we enjoined upon us. According to him, the meaning of the statement is: And We enjoined upon man concerning his parents, and We enjoined upon him goodness. He also said: A man might say, ‘I enjoined upon him goodness,’ meaning, ‘I enjoined upon him goodness.’

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: The meaning of this is: And We have enjoined upon man to do good. However, the Arabs omit some of them from the speech if what remains indicates what was omitted, and they apply what remains to what the omitted acted upon. So he put his statement good in the accusative case even though the meaning is what we described as enjoined, because it has replaced what was omitted.

i: And he recited in this regard: I was amazed at Dahma when he complained about us and at Abu Dahma when he advised us Good for her, as if we had been neglected He said:
x: The meaning of his saying: He advises us to do good is that we should do good to it. So he was satisfied with advising us from it, and he said that similar to his saying: So he began to wipe
r
(Surah Sad: 33)
, meaning he wiped. And His statement: But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them.

That is, We have enjoined upon man, and We said to him: If your parents endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, that I have no partner, then do not obey them and associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, seeking their approval, but he disagreed with them in that. To Me is your return. That is, God Almighty says: To your return and destination on the Day of Resurrection. Then I will inform you of what you used to do. That is, I will inform you of what you used to do in this world of good and bad deeds, then I will reward you for them, the good-doer for goodness, and the evil-doer for what he deserves. It was mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because of Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And We have enjoined upon man, to his parents, good treatment… until His saying:
h
Then I will inform you about what you used to do

. He said: It was revealed about Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas, who had Hajar. His mother said: By God, no house will shelter me until he returns. So God revealed concerning that that he should be good to them and not obey them in polytheism.

x: God Almighty says: And those who believe in God and His Messenger and do righteous deeds - that is, they perform God’s obligations and avoid what He has forbidden - We will surely admit them among the righteous - into the entrance of the righteous, and that is Paradise.
God Almighty says: “
h
And among the people is he who says

, ‘We have acknowledged God, so we believe in Him alone.’ But when the polytheists harm him for his acknowledgment of God, he considers the trial of the people for him in this world to be like the punishment of God in the Hereafter, so he turns away from his faith in God, returning to disbelief in Him. “And if victory comes from your Lord,” O Muhammad, the people of faith in Him, they will surely say, these apostates from their faith, who make the trial of the people to be like the punishment of God, Indeed, we were with you, O believers, giving you victory over your enemies, a lie and a slander. God says, Is not God more knowing, O people, than everyone, of what is in the breasts of the worlds, all of His creation, those who say, We believe in God, and others. So when he is harmed for the sake of God, he turns away from the religion of God.
How can he deceive someone from whom nothing is hidden, and from whom nothing is hidden, secretly or openly? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And of the people is he who says

, ‘We believe in God,’ but when he is harmed for the sake of God, he considers the trial of the people to be like the punishment of God. He said: His trial is that he turns away from the religion of God if he is harmed for the sake of God.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: But when harm is caused for the sake of God, He considers the trial of the people to be like the punishment of God… until His statement:
h
And that He may make known the hypocrites

, he said: People who believe with their tongues, but when a calamity from God or a disaster befalls them in themselves, they are tempted, so they consider that in this world to be like the punishment of God in the Hereafter.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: His statement:
h
And among the people is he who says

, ‘We believe in God’… the verse, was revealed about some hypocrites in Mecca who used to believe, but when they were harmed and afflicted by calamity at the hands of the polytheists, they returned to disbelief for fear of being harmed, and they considered the harm caused by people in this world to be equivalent to the punishment of God.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, But when he is harmed for the sake of God, he considers the trial of the people to be like the punishment of God, he said: He is the hypocrite who, when he is harmed for the sake of God, turns away from the religion and disbelieves, and considers the trial of the people to be like the punishment of God. He mentioned that this verse was revealed about a group of believers who were in Mecca. They left as emigrants, but were overtaken and captured. They gave the polytheists what they wanted from them when they were harmed. The report mentioned that:

c: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi told us: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri told us: Muhammad ibn Sharik told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: There were people from Mecca who had converted to Islam, and they were hiding their Islam. The polytheists expelled them with them on the day of Badr, and some of them were wounded and some were killed. The Muslims said: These companions of ours were Muslims and were forced, so they asked forgiveness for them. Then the verse was revealed:
h
Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves - the angels will say, In what were you?
r
(An-Nisa’: 97)

... to the end of the verse. He said: So he wrote to those Muslims who remained in Mecca with this verse that they had no excuse, so they went out, and the polytheists caught up with them and subjected them to temptation. Then this verse was revealed about them:
h
And of the people is he who says, We believe in God, but when he is harmed for the sake of God, he considers the persecution of the people to be like the punishment of God...
... to the end of the verse. So the Muslims wrote to them about Surat al-Ankabut 29:10
h
And among the people is he who says

, "We believe in God," but when he is harmed for the cause of God, he considers the persecution of the people to be like the punishment of God. But if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, "Indeed, we were with you." Is not God most knowing of what is in the hearts of the worlds? that, so they went out and despaired of all good. Then the verse was revealed about them: {Then indeed, your Lord is for those who emigrated after they had “Be tested, then strive and be patient. Indeed, your Lord, thereafter, is Forgiving and Merciful.” (al-Nahl 16:110) So they wrote to them about that: God has made a way out for you, so they went out. The polytheists caught up with them and fought them until those who escaped were saved, and those who were killed were killed. Bishr told us, he said:

c: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And of the people is he who says
, ‘We believe in God,’ but when he is harmed for the sake of God… to his statement,
h
and that He may make known the hypocrites
, he said: These verses were revealed concerning the people whom the polytheists drove back to Mecca, and these ten verses are Medinan up to here and the rest are Meccan.

x: God Almighty says: And God will surely make known the friends of God, and His party, the people of faith in God among you, O people, and He will surely make known the hypocrites among you until He distinguishes each group among you from the other group, by God making that known among you through trials, tribulations, and tests, and by the hastening of those among you who hasten to emigrate from the land of polytheism to the land of Islam, and the hesitation of those among you who are hesitant to emigrate from it.

God Almighty says: And those who disbelieved among the Quraysh said to those among them who believed in God, Follow our way. That is, they said, “Be like us in denying the resurrection after death and denying reward and punishment for deeds. “And We will bear your sins.” That is, they said, If you follow our way in that, and are resurrected after death and are rewarded for your deeds, then we will bear the burden of your sins at that time. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
Follow our way and we will bear your sins

, he said: The statement of the infidels of Quraysh in Mecca to those among them who believed, he said: They said: We will not be sent, nor will you, so follow us. If you have anything against us, then it is upon us.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Mu’adh say: Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak regarding His statement,
h
And those who disbelieved said
, meaning the leaders among the disbelievers, who said to those among the followers who believed: Leave the religion of Muhammad and follow our religion. This, I mean His statement,
h
Follow our path and we will bear your sins

, even if it was issued in the form of a command, then it contains an interpretation of recompense, and its meaning is what I said: If you follow our path, we will bear your sins, as the poet said: I said, Call and call, for the most beautiful voice is when two callers call. He wants: I pray and I will pray, and its meaning is: If you pray, I will pray. And His statement, “
h
And they will not bear any of their sins
. Indeed, they are liars.” This is a denial from God to the polytheists who said to those who believed,
h
Follow our way and we will bear your sins

. God Almighty says: And they lied in what they said to them. They will not bear any of their sins. Indeed, they are liars in what they said to them and promised them, of bearing their sins if they followed them.

x: God Almighty says: And those who associate others with God, who say to those who believe in Him, Follow our path and we will bear your sins, will bear the burdens of their own souls and the sins of those they led astray and obstructed from the path of God, along with their own burdens. And they will be asked on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to lie to them about in this world, about their false promises to them, and about their saying to them, Follow our path and we will bear your sins, and they fabricated lies about that. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And they will bear their burdens meaning their sins, and burdens in addition to their burdens meaning: the burdens of those they led astray.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And they will bear their own burdens and other burdens along with their own burdens
, and he recited His statement, “
h
That they will bear their own burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection and some of the burdens of those whom they misled without knowledge
. Unquestionably, evil is that which they bear” (al-Nahl 16:25). He said: So this is His statement, and other burdens along with their own burdens.

x: This is a threat from God Almighty to those polytheists from Quraysh, who said to those who believed: Follow our path, and we will bear your sins. He says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not be sad, O Muhammad, about the harm you and your companions will suffer from these polytheists, for even if I grant them respite and prolong their respite, their fate will be ruin, and your fate and the fate of your companions will be elevation and victory over them, and salvation from the punishment that will befall them, just as We did with Noah, when We sent him to his people. He remained among them for a thousand years less fifty years, calling them to monotheism and to abandon the gods and idols. But his calling them to God did nothing to increase their turning to Him and accepting the advice that he brought them from God except to flee. He mentioned that he was sent to his people when he was three hundred and fifty years old.

c: Nasr bin Ali Al-Jahdhami told us: Noah bin Qais told us: Awn bin Abi Shaddad told us:
m: God sent Noah to his people when he was three hundred and fifty years old. He stayed among them for one thousand years, minus fifty years. Then he lived after that for three hundred and fifty years. Then the flood took them. God Almighty says: So abundant water destroyed them. Every abundant water that spreads and overflows is a flood among the Arabs, whether it is a torrent or something else. Likewise, death, if it is widespread and abundant, is also a flood among them. From this comes the saying of the rajaz poet: A devastating flood of death swept them away. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then the flood overtook them
, he said: It is the water that was sent upon them.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: The flood means drowning. And his saying, And they are wrongdoers, means: And they are wronging themselves by their disbelief.

x: God Almighty says: So We saved Noah and the companions of his ship, who were those whom he carried in his ship from his children and their wives. We have explained this before, and mentioned the narrations about it, so there is no need to repeat it in this place. And We made it a sign for the worlds. He says: And We made the ship in which We saved him and his companions a lesson and a gift for the worlds, and an argument against them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
So We saved him and the companions of the ship
... the verse. He said: God left it as a sign for the people at the top of al-Judi.

x: If it were said: The meaning of And We made it a sign for the worlds is And We made Our punishment for them a sign for the worlds, and the ha and the alif in his statement And We made it were made a metaphor for punishment or wrath, and the like, since that had been mentioned previously in his statement, So the flood overtook them while they were wrongdoers, that would be one way of interpretation.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “And also remember, O Muhammad, Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, when he said to his al-Nas 114:‘Worship God, O people, and not any other idols or statues, for you have no other god but Him, and fear Him.’” He says: “And fear His wrath by performing His obligations and avoiding disobeying Him. ‘That is better for you, if you only knew’ what is better for you than what is bad for you.”
God Almighty says, informing about what His friend Abraham said to his al-Nas 114:You people only worship idols besides God, meaning an example.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
You only worship idols besides God means statues
. The commentators differed in their interpretation of His statement,
h
And you invent falsehood

x: Some of them said: It means: And you fabricate lies.
Who said that?

c: Ali told us, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And you invent falsehood
, he said: You fabricate a lie.

x: Others said: You say lies.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
And you invent falsehood
, meaning: And you say falsehood.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
h
And you invent falsehood
, meaning: you tell lies.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And you are fabricating falsehood.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And you invent falsehood
, he said: You carve and depict falsehood.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And you invent falsehood
: meaning you make idols.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And you invent falsehood

, the idols that they carve with their own hands. The most correct of the sayings is the one that says: It means: And you fabricate a lie. The meaning of creation has been previously explained in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it here. So the interpretation of the statement is: You only worship idols besides God, and you fabricate lies and falsehood. In fact, in His statement falsehood it is rejected by only, like the saying of the one who says: You only do such and such, and you only do such and such. All the reciters of the regions read and you create falsehood with a light kha’ from His statement and you create and a damma on the lam: from creation.

c: It was reported from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami
m: that he read and you create falsehood with a fatha on the kha’ and a shaddah on the lam from creation. The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is what the reciters of the regions have said, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it. And His statement, Indeed, those you worship other than God do not possess for you any provision, meaning, the Most High, that your idols that you worship cannot provide you with anything. So seek provision from God, meaning, seek provision from God, not from your idols, and you will attain what you seek from that. And worship Him, meaning, humble yourself before Him. And be grateful to Him, for His provision to you and His blessings that He has bestowed upon you. It is said, I thanked Him and I was grateful to Him, which is more eloquent than I thanked Him. And His statement,
h
To Him you will return

, meaning, to God you will return from your worship of death, and He will ask you about what you are doing of your worship of other than Him, while you are His servants and His creation, and you live in His blessings and eat from His provisions.

evidence.text: All the reciters of the regions read and you create falsehood with a light kha’ from His statement and you create and a damma on the lam: from creation.
The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is what the reciters of the regions have said, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.

x: God the Almighty says: And if you, O people, deny Our Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what he called you to of the worship of your Lord, who created you and provided for you, and the disavowal of idols, then groups before you denied their messengers in what the messengers called them to of the truth, so God’s wrath descended upon them and His immediate punishment descended upon them. So your way is the same as their way in what is descending upon you because of your denial of him. And the Messenger has no duty except to convey clearly means: Muhammad has no duty except to convey to you God’s message and to deliver to you what his Lord commanded him to convey to you. What is meant by clear conveyance is that he makes clear to those who hear him what is intended by it and understands what is meant by it.

God the Almighty says: Have they not seen how God begins the creation of things as a little child, then a young boy, then a mature man, then an adult? It is said from this: He began and returned, and began and returned, two expressions with one meaning. And His statement,
h
Then He will return it
, means
h
then He will return it

after its annihilation and decay, just as He began it the first time, a new creation. This is not difficult for Him. Indeed, that, for God, is easy, is easy just as it was easy for Him to begin it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Have they not seen how God originates creation and then repeats it
?: by resurrection after death.

x: And His statement, Say, ‘Travel through the land,’ God Almighty says to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who deny resurrection after death, who reject reward and punishment: Travel through the land and see how God began things and how He created and brought them into existence. Just as He brought them into existence and brought them into existence at the beginning, it was not impossible for Him to bring them into existence at the beginning, so it is not impossible for Him to bring them into existence again. Then God will bring about the final creation, He says: Then God will bring about that final beginning after annihilation. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Say, ‘Travel through the land and observe how He began creation’ - the creation of the heavens and the earth - ‘
h
Then God will produce the final creation
’ - meaning the resurrection after death.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then God will produce the final creation

, he said: It is life after death, which is the resurrection. And His statement, Indeed, God is over all things competent, means that God Almighty says: Indeed, God is able to create all of His creation after its destruction in the same form it was before its destruction, and to do other things that He wills. Nothing He wills is beyond His power.

x: God Almighty says: Then God will create the final creation of His creation after their annihilation. He will punish whomever He wills among them for the crimes he committed during his lifetime, and He will have mercy on whomever He wills among them who repented, believed, and did righteous deeds. And to Him you will be returned. He says: And to Him you will return and be brought back.
As for his saying,
h
And you will not escape Him on earth or in heaven
, Ibn Zayd said about that what:

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And you will not be able to frustrate Him on earth or in heaven

, he said: The people of the earths will not be able to frustrate Him on earth or the people of the heavens in heaven if they disobey Him. And he recited, Not even the weight of an atom in the heavens or on earth, nor anything smaller than that or greater, but that it is in a clear book
r
(Yunus 10:61)

x: Some of the Arab scholars from Basra said about this: You cannot frustrate those on earth, nor can you frustrate those in the heavens.

This is one of the obscure Arabic words because of the pronoun that did not appear in the second sentence. He said: Similar to it is the statement of Hassan ibn Thabit: Who among you insults the Messenger of God, praises him, and supports him?

He meant: And whoever supports and praises him, so he implied who. He said: And the listener might think that the support and praise belong to whom, this apparent meaning is true. And similar to it in speech is: Be more generous than he who came to you and came to your father, and be more generous than he who came to you but did not come to Zayd. You mean: And whoever did not come to Zayd, so the difference in the actions is sufficient from repeating who, as if he said: Whom he satirizes, and who praises him, and who supports him. And from this is the saying of God the Almighty: And whoever is belittled by night and travels by day
r
(Al-Raʿd: 10)

. This statement is more correct in meaning to me than the other statement. If someone said: Its meaning is: And you will not be able to frustrate him on earth, and you will not be able to frustrate him even if you were in the heaven, that would be a correct school of thought.

And His statement, And you have no protector or helper besides God, means: O people, you have no protector or helper besides God to oversee your affairs, nor any helper to defend you against God if He intends evil for you, nor to prevent you from it if He inflicts His punishment upon you.

God Almighty says: And those who disbelieved in God’s proofs, denied His evidence, and rejected meeting Him and coming to Him on the Day of Resurrection, those are the ones who have despaired of My mercy. God Almighty says: Those are the ones who have despaired of My mercy in the Hereafter when they saw what I have prepared for them of punishment. And those are the ones who will have a painful punishment.
How can he object with these verses, from His statement,
h
And if you deny

, then nations before you denied... to His statement, Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe, and he left out the pronoun in His statement, So what was the response of his people? which is from the story of Abraham. And His statement, Indeed, those you worship other than God... to His statement, “So seek provision from God and worship Him and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned.”

He did that because the report of the matter of Noah, Abraham, and their people, and all the messengers and nations mentioned by God in this surah and others, is only a reminder from God Almighty to those whom He begins by mentioning before interrupting with the report, and a warning from Him to them that what happened to them will happen to them, so it is as if it was said in this place: So worship Him and be grateful to Him, to Him you will be returned. So you, the Quraysh, denied your Messenger Muhammad, just as those denied Abraham. Then He replaced So you denied with
h
And if you deny

, then nations before you have denied, since that indicates the report of their denial of their Messenger. Then He returned to the report of Abraham and his people, and completed his story and their story by saying: So what was the answer of his people?

God Almighty says: The only response of the people of Abraham to him when he said to them: Worship God and fear Him. That is better for you, if you only knew. was that some of them said to one another: Kill him or burn him with fire. So they did. They wanted to burn him with fire, so they set fire to him and threw him into it. But God saved him from it and did not let it prevail over him. Rather, He made it cool and safe for him.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And the answer of the people of Abraham was only that they said

, ‘Kill him or burn him.’ So God saved him from the Fire. He said: Ka’b said: I did not burn him except his chains. “Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.” God Almighty says: Indeed in Our saving of Abraham from the Fire, when he was thrown into it while it was blazing, and making it cool and safe for him, there are proofs and arguments for a people who believe in the proofs and arguments when they see and witness.

x: God Almighty says, informing us of what Abraham said to his al-Nas 114:“And Abraham said to his al-Nas 114:O my people, you have only taken idols besides God.” The reciters differed in reading his statement affection between you. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Ash-Sham, and some of the Kufians, read it affection in the accusative case, affection without adding between you in the accusative case.

Some of the Kufians read it as affection between you in the accusative case, adding affection to his statement between you, and lowering between you. It is as if those who read his statement affection in the accusative case directed the meaning of the speech: to Indeed, O people, you have taken idols out of affection between you. So they made inna a single letter, and applied his statement you have taken to the idols, so they lowered it to mean: You have taken them out of affection between you in this worldly life, loving one another in worshipping them, and being kind to one another in serving them, and communicating with one another on their behalf.

Some of the reciters of Mecca and Basra read it as affection between you in the nominative case, adding affection to between, and lowering between. Those who read it like that made in ma two letters, with the interpretation: Indeed, those whom you have taken idols other than God, it is only your affection. For the world, so they raised affection on the report of inna. It may be permissible that they read it that way, raising it by saying inna so that it is a single letter, and the report is finite at his saying you have only taken idols besides God then the report begins and it is said: Your affection for those idols will not benefit you, it is only affection between you in your worldly life, then it is cut off, and if this meaning is intended, the affection is raised by the description by his saying in the worldly life and it may be permissible that they intended by raising the affection, raising it on the pronoun it.

These three readings are close in meaning, because those who took idols as gods to worship, took them as a source of affection among themselves, and they had affection in this worldly life, but then it was cut off from them. So whichever of them the reader reads, he is correct, because the meanings are close, and the reading of each one of them is well-known among the readers of the regions. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: “And he said: ‘You have only taken idols besides God out of affection among yourselves in worldly life.
h
Then on the Day of Resurrection

some of you will disbelieve in others and curse one another.’” He said: Every friendship in this world will become enmity for its people on the Day of Resurrection, except the friendship of the righteous. And His statement,
h
Then on the Day of Resurrection
, some of you will disbelieve in others and curse each other, God Almighty says:
h
Then on the Day of Resurrection

, O you who love each other in worshipping idols and statues, and who continue to serve them when you come to your Lord and witness the painful torment that God has prepared for you in this world through your mutual love and affection, some of you will disbelieve in each other: He says: Some of you will disown each other and curse each other. And His statement, And your refuge is the Fire, God Almighty says: And the destination of all of you, O idol worshippers and what you worship, is the Fire. And you will have no helpers, He says: And you, O people who have taken gods other than God, have no love among yourselves, no helpers to help you against God when He burns you in the Fire of Hell, and save you from His punishment.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in reading his statement affection between you.
