The majority of the reciters of Medina and Ash-Sham, and some of the Kufians, read it affection in the accusative case, affection without adding between you in the accusative case.
Some of the Kufians read it as affection between you in the accusative case, adding affection to his statement between you, and lowering between you.
Some of the reciters of Mecca and Basra read it as affection between you in the nominative case, adding affection to between, and lowering between.
Those who read it like that made in ma two letters, with the interpretation: Indeed, those whom you have taken idols other than God, it is only your affection.

It may be permissible that they read it that way, raising it by saying inna so that it is a single letter, and the report is finite at his saying you have only taken idols besides God then the report begins and it is said: Your affection for those idols will not benefit you, it is only affection between you in your worldly life, then it is cut off, and if this meaning is intended, the affection is raised by the description by his saying in the worldly life and it may be permissible that they intended by raising the affection, raising it on the pronoun it.
So whichever of them the reader reads, he is correct, because the meanings are close, and the reading of each one of them is well-known among the readers of the regions.

x: God Almighty says: So Abraham, the friend of God, believed Lot, and said, ‘Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord.’ He says: And Abraham said: I am emigrating from the home of my people to my Lord, to Syria. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
So Lot believed him
, he said: Lot spoke the truth, and said, ‘Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord,’ he said: He is Abraham.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
So Lot believed him

, meaning, Lot believed him, and said, ‘Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord,’ he said: They both emigrated from Kutha, which is one of the plains of Kufa, to Ash-Sham. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say, “There will be migration after migration, when the people of the earth will move to the place of migration of Abraham, but the worst of its people will remain on the earth until it spits them out, defiles them, and gathers them into the Fire with the apes and pigs.”

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
So Lot believed him

, he said: Lot believed him, Abraham believed him. He said: Have you seen the believers, did they not believe in what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought? He said: So belief is confirmation. And regarding His statement, Indeed, I will emigrate to my Lord, he said: His emigration was to Syria. Ibn Zayd said in the hadith, “The wolf that spoke to the man, so he told the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: So I, Abu Bakr, and Umar believed him, but neither Abu Bakr nor Umar was with him.” Meaning, I believed him: I believed him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding His statement,
h
So Lot believed him and said
, ‘Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord,’ he said: To Harran. Then he was ordered to go to Ash-Sham, to which Abraham had emigrated, and he was the first to emigrate. He says,
h
So Lot believed him and said
, ‘Indeed, I am emigrating,’... the verse.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
So Lot believed him and said

, ‘Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord,’ that it refers to Abraham who said: Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord. And His statement, Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise, means: Indeed, my Lord is the Exalted in Might who does not humiliate those whom He supports. Rather, He protects them from those who wish to harm them, and to Him is their migration. He is the Wise in His management of His creation and His disposition of them in whatever way He disposes of them.

x: God Almighty says: And We gave him from Ourselves Isaac, a son, and Jacob, after him, a son, a son.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told us, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We gave him Isaac and Jacob
, he said: They are the sons of Abraham. His statement,
h
And We placed among his descendants prophethood and the Book
, means the plural, meaning the Books, but it was used in the same way as their saying, The dirham and dinar became plentiful with so-and-so. And His statement,
h
And We gave him his reward in this world

, means, the Most High, the Majestic, says: And We gave him the reward for his suffering for Us in this world. He in addition to that, in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous. So there he will also have the reward of the righteous, and his share will not be diminished by what he was given in this world of reward for his suffering for God, in relation to what he will have with Him in the Hereafter. It was said: The reward that God Almighty mentioned that He gave to Abraham in this world is good praise and a righteous son.

x: Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And We gave him his reward in this world
. He said: Praise.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Layth, he said:
m: Mujahid sent a man called Qasim to Ikrimah asking him about the statement of God,
h
And We gave him his reward in this world

, and indeed, in the Hereafter, he will be among the righteous. He said: He said, His reward in this world is that every religion supports him, and he is among the righteous in the sight of God. He said: So he returned to Mujahid and said: He hit the nail on the head.

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Mandil, on the authority of someone
m: who mentioned it, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
And We gave him his reward in this world
. He said: The righteous son and praise.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
And We gave him his reward in this world
, meaning: good mention.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We gave him his reward in this world

, he said: Well-being, righteous deeds, and good praise. I will not find anyone from the religions who does not see Abraham and support him. And indeed, in the Hereafter, he will be among the righteous.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And mention Lot, when he said to his al-Nas 114:You indeed commit males, and no one among the worlds has ever done such a thing before you meaning the immorality they were committing, which is committing males. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Khalid bin Khidash and Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ismail bin Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar,
m: regarding His statement, Indeed, you commit an immorality such as no one before you has committed before anyone in the world, he said: No male had intercourse with another male until the people of Lot.

x: God Almighty says, informing about what Lot said to his al-Nas 114:You people, you approach men from behind and you block the way. He says: You block travelers with your evil actions. This is because, according to what was mentioned about them, they used to do that to any travelers who passed by them, or to strangers who came to their country.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And you cut off the way, he said: The way is the road. When a traveler passes by them, and he is a wayfarer, they cut him off and do that evil deed to him. And His statement,
h
And you commit evil in your gatherings

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the evil that God meant, which these people were committing in their gatherings.
Some of them said: It was because they were defecating in their gatherings.
Who said that?

c: Abdul Rahman bin Al-Aswad told me, he said: Muhammad bin Rabi’ah told us, he said: Ruh bin Atifa Al-Thaqafi told us, on the authority of Amr bin Mus’ab, on the authority of Urwah bin Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Aishah,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And you commit evil in your assemblies
, he said: Flatulence.

x: Others said: Rather, it was because they were deleting those who passed by them.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb and Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Hatim ibn Abi Saghira, on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Umm Hani’, who said:
m: “I asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about his statement, ‘
h
And you commit evil in your gatherings
.’ He said: They used to throw stones at the people of the road and make fun of them.” So this was the evil that they used to commit.

c: Al-Rabi’ told us, he said: Asad told us, he said: Abu Usamah told us,
m: with his chain of transmission on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the same.

c: Ahmad bin Abda Al-Dhabi told us: Salim bin Akhdar told us: Abu Yunus Al-Qushayri told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Abu Salih,
m: the freed slave of Umm Hani’, that Umm Hani’ was asked about this verse:
h
And you commit evil in your gatherings
. She said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it, and he said: They used to throw people on the road and make fun of them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Omar bin Abi Zaidah told us:
m: I heard Ikrimah say about His statement,
h
And you commit evil in your gatherings
, he said: They used to harm the people of the road and insult those who passed by them.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: My father told me, on the authority of Omar bin Abi Zaida, he said:
m: I heard Ikrimah say: Deletion.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And you commit evil in your gatherings
. He said: Everyone who passed by them, they would remove him, so he is the evil.

c: Al-Rabi’in narrated to us, saying: Asad narrated to us, saying: Sa’id ibn Zayd narrated to us, saying: Hatim ibn Abi Saghira narrated to us, saying: Samak ibn Harb narrated to us, on the authority of Badham, on the authority of Abu Salih,
m: the freed slave of Umm Hani’, on the authority of Umm Hani’, who said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about this verse:
h
And you commit evil in your gatherings
. He said: They used to sit on the road, and they would pick on wayfarers and make fun of them.

x: Some of them said: Rather, it was their committing of the obscene act in their gatherings.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Some of them would come to each other in their gatherings, meaning his statement,
h
And you commit evil in your gatherings

c: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told us: Thabit ibn Muhammad al-Laythi told us: Fadil ibn Ayyad told us, on the authority of Mansur ibn al-Mu’tamir, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And you commit evil in your gatherings
, he said: Some of them used to have intercourse with each other in gatherings.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And you commit evil in your gatherings
. He said: Some of them would come to each other in gatherings.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told me,
m: on the authority Surat al-Ankabut 29:29 Do you indeed approach men and block the way and commit evil in your assemblies?
h
And the only answer of his people was that they said

, "Bring us the punishment of God, if you should be of the truthful." of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: They used to have sexual intercourse with men in their gatherings.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And you commit in your assemblies evil, he said: gatherings, and evil is their committing men.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And you commit evil in your gatherings
, he said: They used to commit immorality in their gatherings.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And you commit evil in your assemblies

, he said: Their assemblies are the gatherings, and evil is their filthy deeds that they used to do. They would intercept a rider, seize him, and ride him. And he recited, Do you commit immorality while you are seeing? An-Naml 27:54, and he recited, No one has preceded you with it from among the worlds.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And you commit evil in your gatherings

, meaning: in your gatherings. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the one that says: Its meaning is: And you insult those who pass by you in your gatherings, and you make fun of them, based on what we mentioned in the narration on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And His statement,
h
And the only answer of his people was that they said

, ‘Bring us the punishment of God, if you should be of the truthful.’ God Almighty says: The only answer of the people of Lot when he forbade them from what God hates of committing the indecencies that God has forbidden was that they said, Bring us the punishment of God which you threaten us, if you should be of the truthful in what you say and the fulfillers of what you promise.

x: God Almighty says, And when Our messengers came to Abraham with the good tidings from God of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob, they said, ‘Indeed, we are going to destroy the people of this city’ meaning: God’s messengers said to Abraham: “Indeed, we are going to destroy the people of this city, the city of Sodom, which is the city of Lot. “Indeed, its people were wrongdoers” meaning: its people were wronging themselves by disobeying God and denying the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And when Our messengers came to Abraham with the good tidings… to His statement

, We know best who is in it, he said: Abraham argued with the angels about the people of Lot to leave them alone. He said: Have you seen if there are ten houses of Muslims in it, would you leave them alone? The angels said: There are not ten houses in it, nor five, nor four, nor three, nor two. He said: So he grieved for Lot and his family, and said, Indeed, Lot is in it. They said: We know best who is in it. We will surely save him and his family, except for his wife; she was among those who remained behind. This is what He said, “He argues with Us concerning the people of Lot. Indeed, Abraham was forbearing, compassionate, and frequently turning back [to God].”
r

. The angels said: “O Abraham, turn away from this. Indeed, the command of your Lord has come, and there will come upon them a punishment that cannot be averted.” Hud 76 Then God sent Gabriel, peace be upon him, to them, and he blew up the city and everything in it with one of his wings, turning it upside down, and he pursued them with stones in every land.

x: God Almighty says: Abraham said to the messengers from the angels - when they said to him, "Indeed, We will destroy the people of this city. Indeed, its people were wrongdoers," and they did not exclude anyone from them, as they described them as wrongdoers -: There is Lot in it, and he is not among the wrongdoers, rather he is one of the messengers of God, and one of the people of faith in Him, and obedience to Him. So the messengers said to him, We know best who is in it of the wrongdoers who disbelieve in God than you, and Lot is not among them, rather he is, as you said, one of the friends of God, to save him and his family from the destruction that is descending upon the people of his city except his wife, she was among those who remained behind those whom the ages and days kept alive, and their lives and ages were prolonged, and she is to perish from among the people of Lot with her people.
God Almighty says,
h
And when Our messengers came to Lot

from the angels, he was distressed by them. He says: The angels were distressed by their coming to him, because they were his guests, so they distressed him by that. So His saying, he was distressed by them means he did to them what distressed him by that.

c: It was reported on the authority of Qatada
m: that he used to say: He had a bad opinion of his people, and he was very rude to his guest.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us that: Abd al-Razzaq told us that Muammar told us
m: on his authority: And he was fed up with them. He said: He was fed up with their hospitality because he knew of the evil deeds of his people.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Thabit Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And when Our messengers came to Lot

, he was distressed by them and felt straitened for them, he said: with the hospitality, fearing for them because of what he knew of the evil of his people. And His statement, And they said, ‘Do not fear and do not grieve,’ means, The messengers said to Lot, ‘Do not fear for us, lest your people reach us, and do not grieve over what we have told you about who we will destroy.’ That is because the messengers said to him, O Lot, indeed we are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you, so set out with your family during a part of the night
r

. Indeed, We will save you from the punishment that is about to descend upon your people, and your family, meaning, and We will save your family with you, except your wife, for she will perish with those of her people who will perish. She was among those who survived and lived long lives.

x: God Almighty says, informing us of what the messengers said to Lot: We are going to send down, O Lot, upon the people of this city, Sodom, a punishment from the sky, meaning torment.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Indeed, We will send down upon the people of this city a punishment: meaning torment. We have previously explained the meaning of the Rajaz and the statements of the interpreters of the Qur’an, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it here. His saying,
h
Because they were committing sins
, means:
h
Because they were committing sins
against God and committing immoral acts.

x: God Almighty says: And We have certainly left behind from our deed which We did to them a sign, meaning: a clear and admonishing lesson, for a people who understand God’s arguments and reflect on His admonitions. And that clear sign is, in My view, the forgiveness of their traces and the lessons of their landmarks.
It was mentioned on the authority of Qatada regarding this:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And We have certainly left of it a clear sign for a people who understand. He said: It is the stones that were rained down upon them.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, From it is a clear sign, he said: a lesson.

x: God Almighty says: And I sent to Madyan their brother Shuʿayb, and he said to them: O my people, worship God alone, and humble yourselves before Him in obedience, and submit to Him in worship. And hope for the Last Day meaning: And hope through your worship of Me for the reward of the Last Day, which is the Day of Resurrection. And do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption meaning: And do not increase your disobedience to God on the earth, and do not persist in it, but repent to God for it and turn back.

Some scholars of Arabic language interpreted the phrase And hope for the Last Day to mean And fear the Last Day. Other scholars of Arabic language rejected this and said: We do not find hope in the sense of fear in Arabic speech unless it is accompanied by denial.

God Almighty says: So the people of Madyan denied Shu'aib regarding the message he brought them from God, so the trembling of the punishment seized them, and they lay dead within their homes, some of them on top of others.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And they became dead in their homes: meaning dead.

x: God Almighty says: And remember, O people, ‘Aad and Thamud, and it has become clear to you from their dwellings that they were ruined and empty of them because of Our attacks upon them and the descent of Our power upon all of them. And Satan made their deeds pleasing to them meaning: Satan made their disbelief in God and their denial of His messengers seem good to them. So he averted them from the path meaning: He turned them back by making what was pleasing to them of disbelief seem good to them, from the path of God, which is belief in Him and His messengers and what they brought them from their Lord. And they were discerning meaning: They were discerning in their misguidance, admiring it, thinking that they were on the right path and correct, while they were on the path of misguidance. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, my uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And He turned them away from the path
, and they were seeing the truth, meaning: They were seeing the truth in their religion.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told me, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, and they were discerning in misguidance.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And they were discerning in their misguidance, admiring it.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, in his statement, and they were discerning, he said: in their religion.

x: God Almighty says: And remember, O Muhammad, Korah, Pharaoh, and Haman. They all came to Moses with clear proofs, meaning clear signs, but they were arrogant on earth and refused to believe in the clear signs and to follow Moses, peace be upon him. And they were not forerunners: God Almighty says: And they were not forerunners of Us by themselves, so that they would escape Us, but We had power over them.

God Almighty says: So We seized all these nations that We mentioned to you, O Muhammad, with Our punishment. And among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones. They were the people of Lot, upon whom God rained stones of layered baked clay. The Arabs call the violent wind that is in small pebbles, snow, hail, or ice a storm. From this comes the saying of Al-Akhtal: And I knew that when the tithes depart, the hedgehogs throw them northward. The tree throws hail from its snow until it sleeps on the tree, stumbling over it. Al-Farazdaq said: We are receiving the northern Levant, which will be struck by hailstones like scattered cotton. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: And among them were those upon whom We sent a violent storm of stones - the people of Lot.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And among them were those upon whom We sent a violent storm of stones - and they were the people of Lot - And among them were those whom the blast seized.

x: The interpreters differed about who was meant by this.
Some of them said: They are Thamud, the people of Salih.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: And among them were those whom the blast seized - Thamud.

x: Others said: Rather, they are the people of Shuaib.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And among them were those whom the blast seized - the people of Shuaib.

c: The correct thing to say about this is that God has informed us
m: about Thamud and the people of Shuʿayb from the people of Madyan that He destroyed them with the blast in His Book in a place other than this. Then He, the Most High, said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Among the nations We destroyed were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones, and among them were those whom the blast seized. He did not specify in this report some of the nations whom the blast seized over others, and both nations, I mean Thamud and Madyan, were seized by the blast. And His saying,
h
And among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow up
, meaning Qarun. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
b.via: correct thing to say about this is that God has

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: And among them were those whom We drowned were the people of Noah.

x: Others said: Rather, they are the people of Pharaoh.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And among them were those whom We drowned were the people of Pharaoh. The correct thing to say about this is: It refers to the people of Noah, Pharaoh, and his people, because God did not specify one nation over the other, and He had destroyed them before this report was revealed about them, so they are both meant by it. And His statement, And God would not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves, means, the Most High, the Majestic, says: And God would not have destroyed these nations whom He destroyed for the sins of others, thus wronging them by destroying them without their justification. Rather, He destroyed them for their sins, their disbelief in their Lord, and their ingratitude for His blessings upon them, despite His continuous kindness to them and the abundance of His favors upon them. But they were wronging themselves by their misuse of their Lord’s blessings, their turning away from His favors, their worship of other than Him, and their disobedience to the One upon whom He bestowed blessings.

x: God Almighty says: The parable of those who take gods and idols besides God as allies, hoping for their support and benefit when they need them, is that their cunning is weak, their narrative is ugly, and their choices for themselves are bad. It is like the spider in its weakness and lack of cunning. It takes a house for itself, so that it may shelter itself, but it does not avail it at all when it needs it. Likewise, these polytheists were not availed at all when God’s command came upon them and His wrath descended upon them, by their allies whom they took besides God, and they did not ward off from themselves the wrath that God brought upon them by their worship of them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement,
h
The example of those who take protectors other than God is like that of the spider who takes a home… to the end of the verse
. He said: That is an example that God has given for those who worship other than Him. Indeed, his example is like that of the spider’s home.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
The example of those who take protectors other than God is like that of the spider

. He said: This is an example that God gave to the polytheist, the example of his god whom he calls upon other than God is like that of the spider’s web. It is weak and flimsy and will not benefit him.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
The example of those who take protectors other than God is like that of the spider who takes a home

. He said: This is an example that God has given. Their protectors will not avail them at all, just as the spider’s home will not avail them at all. And His statement, And indeed, the flimsiest of houses means: And indeed, the weakest of houses is the spider’s house, if they only knew. God Almighty says: If these people who have taken protectors other than God knew, or their protectors whom they have taken other than God, in their lack of need for them, like the spider’s house’s lack of need for them, but they are ignorant of that, so they think that they are benefiting them and bringing them closer to God.

x: The reciters differed in their reading of His statement Indeed, God knows what you call upon. The majority of the reciters in the regions read it you call upon with a ta’ meaning addressing the polytheists of Quraysh. Indeed, God O people knows what you call upon to other than Him of anything. Abu Amr read it as Indeed, God knows what they call upon with a ya’ meaning reporting about the nations. Indeed, God knows what these nations whom We destroyed call upon other than Him of anything. The correct reading in this regard, in our view, is the reading of those who read with the letter ta’, because if this were report about the nations that God mentioned that He destroyed, the statement would have been: God knows what they were calling for, because the people were not present at the time this report was revealed to the Prophet of God, since they had been destroyed and perished. Rather, it is said: God knows what you are calling for if it is intended to be report about those who are present, not about those who have perished.

The interpretation of the statement, if the matter is as we have described, is: God knows, O people, the condition of whatever you worship besides Him, and that it neither benefits you nor harms you if God intends evil for you, nor does it avail you at all. Indeed, it is like the spider’s web in its lack of need for you. And His statement, And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise, means: And God is the Exalted in Might in His vengeance upon those who disbelieved in Him and associated others with Him in worship. So, you who associate others with Him, fear His punishment by believing in Him before it descends upon you, just as it descended upon the nations whose stories God has related to you in this Surah. For if His punishment descends upon you, your allies whom you have taken as allies other than Him will not benefit you, just as their allies whom they took other than Him did not benefit them before you.

He is the Wise in His management of His creation. So He destroys whomever deserves destruction at the time when his destruction is good, and He delays whomever His creation delays his destruction until the time when his destruction is good.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of His statement Indeed, God knows what you call upon.
The majority of the reciters in the regions read it you call upon with a ta’ meaning addressing the polytheists of Quraysh.
Abu Amr read it as Indeed, God knows what they call upon with a ya’ meaning reporting about the nations.

The correct reading in this regard, in our view, is the reading of those who read with the letter ta’, because if this were report about the nations that God mentioned that He destroyed, the statement would have been: God knows what they were calling for, because the people were not present at the time this report was revealed to the Prophet of God, since they had been destroyed and perished.

x: And His statement,
h
And these examples We present to the people

, God Almighty says: And these examples, which are the likenesses and parallels, We present to the people. He says: We give examples of them and make them similar and use them as evidence for the people, as Al-A’sha said: Do you remember the covenant of Tanmas when you gave me an example of sitting there? None will comprehend it except those of knowledge. God Almighty says: None will comprehend that they have been afflicted with these examples that We present to the people, and that they have the truth and correctness in what I have presented as an example, except those of knowledge about God and His signs.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: God, O Muhammad, created the heavens and the earth alone, and He is the only One who created them. No partner shares with Him in their creation. Indeed in that is a sign. He says that in His creation is an argument for whoever believes in the arguments when he witnesses them, and the signs when he sees them.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Recite meaning read what has been revealed to you of the Book, meaning what was sent down to you from this Qur’an, and establish prayer meaning: perform the prayer that God has imposed upon you within its limits. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the prayer mentioned in this place.
Some of them said: It means the Qur’an that is recited in the place of prayer, or during prayer.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Abu al-Wafa, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Umar:
m: Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing. He said: The Qur’an that is recited in the mosques.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant prayer.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, meaning: In prayer there is a limit and a deterrent from the sins of God.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Khalid bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Al-Ala bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of someone
m: who mentioned it, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing. Whoever’s prayer does not prohibit immorality and wrongdoing, his prayer only increases his distance from God.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Khalid told us, he said:
m: Al-Ala’ bin Al-Musayyab said, on the authority of Samra bin Atiyah, he said: It was said to Ibn Masoud, So-and-so prays a lot. He said: It only benefits the one who obeys it. He said: Al-Husayn told us, he said:

c: Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Malik bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Yazid, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said:
m: He whose prayer does not command him to do good and forbid him from evil, will only increase his distance from God. He said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said:

c: Ali ibn Hashim ibn al-Barid narrated to us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Masʿud, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: There is no prayer for one who does not obey the prayer, and obedience to the prayer is that it forbids indecency and wrongdoing. He said: Sufyan said: They said, ‘O Shuʿayb, does your prayer command you?’
r

. He said: Sufyan said: Yes, by God, it commands him and forbids him. Ali said: Ismail bin Muslim narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever performs a prayer that does not forbid him from indecency and wrongdoing, will only increase his distance from God.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: If prayer does not prevent him from indecency and wrongdoing, he said: Whoever’s prayer prevents him from indecency and wrongdoing, he will only increase in distance from God.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada and Al-Hasan, they said:
m: He whose prayer does not prevent him from indecency and wrongdoing, will only increase his distance from God by doing so. The correct thing to say about this is that prayer prevents indecency and wrongdoing, as Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masoud said.

x: How does prayer prevent indecency and wrongdoing if what is recited in it is not intended?
It prevents whoever is in it, and prevents him from committing indecencies, because his preoccupation with it prevents him from being preoccupied with wrongdoing.

For this reason, Ibn Masʿud said: Whoever does not obey his prayer will only grow further from God. This is because his obedience to it means his establishment of its limits, and in his obedience to it he is deterred from indecency and wrongdoing.

c: Abu Hamid al-Himsi told us: Yahya ibn Saeed al-Attar told us: Arta’ah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn,
m: regarding the statement of God, Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, he said: When you are praying, then you are doing good, and it has kept you from immorality and wrongdoing. Immorality is adultery, and wrongdoing is disobeying God. Whoever commits an immorality or disobeys God in his prayer in a way that invalidates his prayer, then there is no doubt that his prayer is invalid. And his saying,
h
And the remembrance of God is greater

x: The people of interpretation differed in its interpretation.
Some of them said: Its meaning is: And Surat al-Ankabut 29:45 Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing,
h
and the remembrance of God is greater
. And God knows that which you do. God’s remembrance of you is better than His remembrance of you.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hisham narrated to us, saying: Ata ibn as-Sa’ib informed us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Rabi’ah, who said:
m: Ibn Abbas said to me: Do you know what is meant by His statement,
h
And the remembrance of God is greater

? I said: Yes. He said: What is it? I said: Tasbeeh, tahmeed, and takbeer in prayer, and reciting the Qur’an and the like. He said: You have said something strange, but it is not like that. Rather, He only says: God’s remembrance of you when He has commanded or forbidden something, if you remember Him, is greater than your remembrance of Him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Ibn Rabi’ah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: God’s remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Abdullah bin Rabi’ah, who said:
m: Ibn Abbas asked me about the statement of God,
h
And the remembrance of God is greater

, so I said: Remembrance of Him through glorification, magnification, and the Qur’an is good, but remembrance of Him when performing forbidden acts is one’s abstention from them. He said: You have said something amazing, but it is not as you said, but God’s remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Rabi’ah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
And the remembrance of God is greater
. He said: God’s remembrance of the servant is better than his remembrance of him.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Wakee’ told us.
m: Ibn al-Muthanna said: Abd al-A’la told me. Ibn Wakee’ said: Abd al-A’la told us. He said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, who said: I was sitting with Ibn Abbas when a man came and asked Ibn Abbas about the remembrance of God being greater. Ibn Abbas said: Prayer and fasting. He said: That is the remembrance of God. A man said: I left a man in my house who said something other than this. He said:
h
And the remembrance of God is greater
. He said: God’s remembrance of His servants is greater than the servants’ remembrance of Him. Ibn Abbas said: By God, your companion has spoken the truth.
b.via: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Wakee’

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said:
m: A man came to Ibn Abbas and said: Tell me about the statement of God,
h
And the remembrance of God is greater
. He said: God’s remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: h
And the remembrance of God is greater
. He said: God’s remembrance of the servant is better than his remembrance of Him.

c: Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us: Ibn Fadil told us: Fadil bin Marzouq told us, on the authority of Atiyah:
m: h
And the remembrance of God is greater
. He said: It is His saying: So remember Me, and I will remember you (al-Baqarah 2:152). And God’s remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And the remembrance of God of His servants when they remember Him is greater than your remembrance of Him.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
h
And the remembrance of God is greater
, he said: The remembrance of God by His servant is greater than the servant’s remembrance of his Lord in prayer or otherwise.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Musa, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: God’s remembrance of you when you remember Him is greater than your remembrance of Him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Abu Qurra, on the authority of Salman,
m: the same. Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i narrated: Abu Usamah narrated: Abdul Hamid bin Ja’far narrated: Salih bin Abi Urayb narrated: Kathir bin Murrah Al-Hadrami narrated: I heard Abu Darda’ say: “Shall I not tell you of the best of your deeds, the most beloved to your Lord, the most elevating of your ranks, better than attacking your enemy and striking their necks, and better than giving dinars and dirhams?” They said: What is it? He said: Remembrance of your Lord, and remembrance of God is greater.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: My father told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Aamer, he said:
m: I asked Abu Qurrah about his statement,
h
And the remembrance of God is greater

. He said: God’s remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him. He said: My father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid and Ikrimah, who said: God’s remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him. He said: Hassan bin Ali told us, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Abdullah,
h
And the remembrance of God is greater

. He said: The servant’s remembrance of God is greater than the servant’s remembrance of his Lord. He said: Abu Yazid al-Razi narrated to us, on the authority of Yaʿqub, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Shuʿbah, who said: God’s remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And your remembrance of God is better than everything.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Amr ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of al-Aizar ibn Harith, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Salman, on the authority of someone
m: who was asked: Which deed is best? He said: Do you not read the Qur’an:
h
And the remembrance of God is greater
: There is nothing better than the remembrance of God.

c: Ibn Hamid Ahmad ibn al-Mughira al-Himsi told us: Ali ibn Ayyash told us: al-Layth told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Rabia ibn Yazid, on the authority of Ismail ibn Ubayd God, on the authority of Umm al-Darda’, that she said:
m: h
And the remembrance of God is greater

. So if you pray, then it is from the remembrance of God, and if you fast, then it is from the remembrance of God, and every good thing that you do is from the remembrance of God, and every evil thing that you avoid is from the remembrance of God, and the best of that is glorifying God.

c: Bushran told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And the remembrance of God is greater
. He said: There is nothing greater than the remembrance of God. He said: The greatest of all things. And he recited: Establish prayer for My remembrance
r
(Ta-Ha: 14)
. He said: For the remembrance of God. And he did not describe it during battle except that it is greater.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said:
m: A man said to Salman: Which deed is best? He said: Remembrance of God.

x: Others said: It is possible for both aspects, meaning the first statement that we mentioned and the second.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And the remembrance of God is greater
, he said: It has two aspects: The remembrance of God is greater than anything else, and God’s remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Ismail bin Ibrahim told us, he said: Khalid Al-Hadha’ told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding
h
And the remembrance of God is greater
, he said: It has two aspects: God’s remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him, and God’s remembrance when He has forbidden.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: The servant’s remembrance of God in prayer is greater than the prayer itself.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And the remembrance of God is greater
, he said: The servant’s remembrance of God in prayer is greater than prayer.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: The prayer that you performed, and your remembrance of God in it, is greater than what the prayer forbade of indecency and wrongdoing.

c: Ahmad bin Al-Mughira Al-Himsi told me: Yahya bin Saeed Al-Attar told us: Arta’ah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn,
m: regarding the statement of God, Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and what you are doing of remembrance of God is greater.

x: The most similar of these statements to what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the revelation is the statement of the one who said: And God’s remembrance of you is better than your remembrance of Him. And His statement,
h
And God knows what you do

, means: God knows what you do, O people, in your prayers, in terms of establishing its limits, and abandoning that and other matters of yours, and He will reward you for that. He says: So beware of neglecting any of its limits, and God knows best.

evidence.text: Some of them said: It means the Qur’an that is recited in the place of prayer, or during prayer.
He said: The Qur’an that is recited in the mosques.
If someone were to say: How does prayer prevent indecency and wrongdoing if what is recited in it is not intended?

Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Abu Qurra, on the authority of Salman, the same.

x: God Almighty says: And do not argue O believers in God and His Messenger, with the Jews and Christians, who are the People of the Scripture, except in a way that is best meaning: except with beautiful speech, which is calling to God with His verses and pointing out His proofs. And His statement,
h
Except those among them who are unjust
, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation.

Some of them said: Its meaning is: Except those who refused to acknowledge with you the payment of the jizya, and set up war against you in order to do so, for they are unjust. So argue with them with the sword until they submit or pay the jizya.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Sahl told me, he said: Yazid told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best
, except for those who commit injustice among them, he said: Whoever fights and does not pay the jizyah.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told me, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar. However, he said: Whoever fights you and does not pay you the jizyah.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best
he said: If they say evil, then say good, except for those who do wrong among them then take revenge on them.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Except those among them who do wrong, he said: They said: There is a god with God, or He has a son, or He has a partner, or God’s hand is chained, or God is poor, or they harmed Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: They are the People of the Book.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed:
m: h
And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best
, except for those who commit injustice among them. He said: The people of war, those who have no covenant, argue with him with the sword.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: And do not argue with the People of the Scripture who believed in him and followed his Messenger in what they told you about in their books except in a way that is best, except for those who commit injustice among them. So they persisted in their disbelief. They said: This verse is decisive and has not been abrogated.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God,
h
And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best

, he said: It is not abrogated. You should not argue with those who have believed among them, for perhaps they may agree on something in the Book of God that you do not know, so do not argue with them. And you should not argue with anyone except those who have wronged, those among them who remain steadfast in their religion. So he said: He is the one who argues, and it is said to him, With the sword. He said: And these are Jews. He said: There were no Christians in the land of emigration. It was only the Jews who spoke to and sided with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And Nadir betrayed the Day of Uhud, and Qurayza betrayed the Day of the Confederates.

x: Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed before the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to fight. They said: It was abrogated by His statement:
h
Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day (al-Tawbah 9
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best

, then it was abrogated after that, and he ordered fighting them in Surat Bara’ah, and there is no argument more severe than the sword, that they should be fought until they testify that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or they agree to pay the tax. The most correct of these statements is the statement Surat al-Ankabut 29:46
h
And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best

, except for those who commit injustice among them, and say, "We believe in that which was revealed to us and revealed to you. And our God and your God is one; and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him." of the one who said: What he meant by his statement, except those among them who were unjust, is except for those who refused to pay the jizya and waged war against it.

x: Or is there anyone among the People of the Book who is not a wrongdoer, except for those who do not pay the jizyah?

“Even though all of them are wrongdoers to themselves by their disbelief in God and their denial of His Messenger Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), He did not mean by His statement, ‘except for those among them who are wrongdoers,’ wronging themselves. Rather, He meant by it, ‘except for those among them who are wrongdoers who are the people of faith in God and His Messenger Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), for those argued with them by means of fighting.” Rather, we said: This is the most correct of the sayings about it, because God, the Most High, mentioned that He permitted the believers to argue with the oppressors among the People of the Book in a way that is not best, by His saying,
h
Except for those among them who commit injustice

. So it is known that since He permitted them to argue with them, those who were not permitted to argue with them except in a way that is best are not those among them who were permitted to do so, and that they are not the believers, because it is not permissible to argue with a believer among them except in a way that is not right, because if he comes with something other than the truth, then the oppressors will hear me in what he contradicted the truth. Since this is the case, it becomes clear that there is no meaning to the statement of those who said that what he meant by His saying,
h
And do not argue with the People of the Book is the believers among them

Likewise there is no meaning to the statement of those who said that this verse was revealed before the command to fight, and claimed that it was abrogated, because there is no report of that that would cut off the excuse, nor is there any evidence of its correctness from the innate mind. We have explained in more than one place in our book that it is not permissible to rule that God’s ruling in His Book has been abrogated except by an argument that must be accepted, whether it is a report or reason. And His statement, “And say, ‘We believe in that which has been revealed to us and revealed to you. And our God and your God is one, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him.’” God Almighty says to those who believe in Him and in His Messenger, whom He forbade from arguing with the People of the Book except in a way that is best: If the People of the Book tell you, O people, about their books, and inform you about them of what it is possible and possible that they may be truthful in it, or that they may be lying in it, and you do not know their situation and their state in that, then say to them, We believe in that which has been revealed to us and revealed to you, of what is in the Torah and the Gospel.

And our God and your God is one, meaning: and our God and your God is one. And we are Muslims [in submission] to Him, meaning: and we are submissive and humble to Him in obedience to what He has commanded and forbidden us. In a similar vein to what we have said, there is a report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
The narration mentions this: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated: Uthman ibn Umar narrated:

c: Ali informed us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said:
m: The People of the Book used to read the Torah in Hebrew, and then explain it in Arabic for the Muslims. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not believe the People of the Book and do not disbelieve them, but say: ‘We believe in that which was revealed to us and revealed to you. Our God and your God is one, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him.’”

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Asim told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Saʿd ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of ʿAtaʿ ibn Yasar, who said:
m: Some Jews were talking to some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: “Do not believe them and do not disbelieve them, but say: ‘We believe in that which was revealed to us and that which was revealed to you.’” He said: Abu Amir told us, he said:

c: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Amara bin Umair, on the authority of Harith bin Zuhair, on the authority of Abdullah, he said:
m: Do not ask the People of the Book about anything, for they will not guide you and they have gone astray. Either you deny the truth or you believe in falsehood, for there is no one among the People of the Book who does not have in his heart a desire that calls him to his religion, just as the desire for money. Mujahid used to say about this:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, and Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa’ both narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Except for those among them who have wronged

, he said: They said, There is a god with God, or He has a son, or He has a partner, or The hand of God is chained, or God is poor, or They harmed Muhammad, “And say, ‘We believe in that which was revealed to us and revealed to you,’” for those among the People of the Book who did not say this.

x: God Almighty says: Just as We sent down the Book to those before you, O Muhammad, of the Messengers, Likewise We sent down to you this “Book. So those to whom We gave the Book “before you from the Children of Israel” believe in it, and among these are those who believe in it.” He says: And among these who are among you today are those who believe in it, such as Abdullah bin Salam, and those who believed in him and his Messenger from the Children of Israel. And His statement,
h
None denies Our signs except the disbelievers
, God Almighty says: None denies Our proofs and arguments except he who denies Our blessings upon him and denies Our Oneness and Lordship, knowingly and out of defiance of Us.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: None reject Our signs except the disbelievers. He said: Denial only occurs after knowledge.

x: God Almighty says: And you, O Muhammad, did not recite meaning you read before it meaning before this Book that I revealed to you of any Book, nor did you inscribe it with your right hand meaning: And you were not writing with your right hand, but you were unlettered then the falsifiers would have had doubts meaning: And if you had been, before revelation came to you, reading the Book, or writing it with your right hand, then they would have had doubts: meaning: Then because of that, they would have doubted about your matter, and what you brought to them from your Lord of this Book that you recite to them, the falsifiers who say that it is rhyme and divination, and that it is legends of the ancients. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, “
h
And you did not recite before it any scripture
, nor did you inscribe it with your right hand. Then the falsifiers would have had doubts.” He said: He was illiterate, and the illiterate is the one who does not write.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, And you did not recite before it any book, nor did you inscribe it with your right hand, he said: The Prophet of God did not read a book before it, nor did he inscribe it with his right hand. He said: He was illiterate, and the illiterate is the one who does not write.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Idris Al-Awdi, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And you did not recite before it any scripture

, nor did you inscribe it with your right hand. He said: The People of the Book found in their books that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not write with his right hand, nor did he read a book, so this verse was revealed. And in a similar manner to what we also said regarding his statement,
h
Then the falsifiers would have doubted
, they said.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Then the falsifiers would have doubted
. Then they would have said: This is only something that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, learned and wrote.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God,
h
Then the falsifiers would have doubted
, he said: Quraysh.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of his statement, Rather, they are clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge.

Some of them said: It refers to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They said: The meaning of the statement is: Rather, the existence of the People of the Book in their books that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, neither writes nor reads, and that he is illiterate, are clear signs in their breasts.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, Rather, they are clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge, he said: God, the Most High, had revealed the status of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Torah and the Gospel for the people of knowledge and taught him to them, and made him a sign for them, so He said to them: The sign of his prophethood is that when he emerges he will not know a book, nor write it with his right hand, and these are the clear signs.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And you did not recite before it any book, that the Prophet of God did not read or write, and thus God described him in the Torah and the Gospel, that he was an illiterate prophet who did not read or write, and this is the clear sign in the hearts of those who were given knowledge.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Rather, they are clear signs in the breasts of those who were given knowledge from the People of the Book who believed in Muhammad, his description, and his prophethood.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: Rather, they are clear signs. He said: God revealed the status of Muhammad in the Torah and the Gospel for the people of knowledge. Rather, he is a clear sign in the hearts of those who have been given knowledge. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said.

x: Others said: He meant the Qur’an by that, and they said: The meaning of the words is: Rather, this Qur’an is clear verses in the hearts of those who were given knowledge among the believers in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said:
m: Al-Hasan said, regarding His statement: Rather, they are clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge, the Qur’an is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge, meaning the believers. The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the one that says: What he meant by that is: Rather, the knowledge that you did not recite before this book a book, nor did you write it with your right hand, are clear signs in the hearts of those who were given knowledge from among the People of the Book. I said that this is the more correct of the two interpretations of the verse, because His statement, Rather, they are clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge, is between two pieces of report from God about His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So it is more appropriate for it to be report about him than it is for it to be report about the book about which the report has already been said. And His statement, None reject Our signs except the wrongdoers, God Almighty says: None reject the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his proofs, and deny the knowledge that is taught from the books of God that He revealed to His prophets, regarding the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his prophethood and mission, except the wrongdoers, meaning those who wronged themselves by their disbelief in God Almighty.

x: God the Almighty says: The polytheists of Quraysh said: Why was a sign not sent down to Muhammad from his Lord that would be a proof of God against us, just as the she-camel was made a sign for Salih and the table a sign for Jesus? Say, O Muhammad, the signs are only with God; none but He has the power to produce them. And I am only a clear warner. I am only a warner to you, warning you of the punishment of God for your disbelief in His Messenger and what he brought to you from your Lord. Clear means: He has made His warning clear to you.

God Almighty says: Is it not enough for these polytheists, O Muhammad, who say: Why was a sign not sent down to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the signs and proofs, We have sent down to you this Book that is recited to them meaning it is read to them Indeed in that is mercy meaning: Indeed in this Book that We sent down to them is mercy for those who believe in it and a reminder for them to remember what is in it of lessons and admonition. He mentioned that this verse was revealed because some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, copied something from some of the books of the People of the Book.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Yahya ibn Jaʿdah,
m: that some Muslims came to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with books in which they had written some of what the Jews say. When he looked at them, he threw them away and said: It is enough that a people are foolish, or a people are misguided, that they turn away from what their Prophet brought to them, in favor of what someone other than their Prophet brought to a people other than them. So the verse was revealed: Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book which is recited to them? Indeed in that is mercy and a reminder for a people who believe.

evidence.text: God Almighty says: Is it not enough for these polytheists, O Muhammad, who say: Why was a sign not sent down to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the signs and proofs, We have sent down to you this Book that is recited to them meaning it is read to them Indeed in that is mercy meaning: Indeed in this Book that We sent down to them is mercy for those who believe in it and a reminder for them to remember what is in it of lessons and admonition.
So the verse was revealed: Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book which is recited to them?

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who say to you: Why was a sign not sent down to you from your Lord? Those who deny Our signs from your al-Nas 114:God is sufficient, O these people, as a witness between me and you for me and against me, because He knows who is right among us from who is wrong, and He knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth. Nothing in them is hidden from Him. He will reward each group among us according to what is due to them, the one who is right for his steadfastness upon the truth, and the one who is wrong for his falsehood, according to what is due to them. And those who believe in falsehood means: they believed in polytheism, so they acknowledged it and disbelieved in it. He means: and they denied God. Those are the losers means: they are the ones who are cheated in their deal. And similar to what we said about His statement,
h
And those who believed in falsehood
, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And those who believe in falsehood means polytheism.

x: God the Almighty says: And these people of yours urge you, O Muhammad, to hasten you: Why was a sign not sent down to him from his Lord of the punishment? And they say: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky (al-Anfal 8:32) And were it not for a term that I had named for them so that I would not destroy them until they fulfilled it and attained it, the punishment would have come upon them suddenly. And His statement:
h
And it will surely come upon them suddenly while they perceive not

means: And the punishment will come upon them suddenly while they are not aware of the time of its coming before its arrival. And in a manner similar to what we said about that, the people of interpretation.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, And they ask You to hasten the punishment, he said: Some ignorant people of this nation said, O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment (al-Anfal 8:32)... the verse.

x: God Almighty says: O Muhammad, these polytheists are hastening you to bring the punishment upon them, while the Fire is surrounding them and all that remains is for them to enter it. It has also been said that this is the sea.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Samak, who said:
m: I heard ʿIkrimah say about this verse, And indeed, Hell will encompass the disbelievers. He said: The sea.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ghundar told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: the same.

x: God Almighty says, And Hell will surely encompass the disbelievers. The Day the punishment will cover the disbelievers from above them in Hell and from beneath their feet.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: On the Day the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet: meaning in the Fire. And His statement,
h
And He will say

, ‘Taste what you used to do,’ means, The Most High is His praise, and God will say to them, Taste what you used to do in this world of sins against God and what angers Him therein. And with the ya in
h
And He will say

, ‘Taste,’ the majority of the reciters of the regions read it with the ya except for Abu Jaʿfar and Abu ʿAmr, for they both read it with the nun and we say. And the reading that we have is with the ya due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.

evidence.text: And with the ya in And He will say, ‘Taste,’ the majority of the reciters of the regions read it with the ya except for Abu Jaʿfar and Abu ʿAmr, for they both read it with the nun and we say.
And the reading that we have is with the ya due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.

x: God Almighty says to His believing servants:
h
O My servants who have believed
in Me and in My Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, My earth is spacious. The commentators differed about the meaning intended by the report about the vastness of the earth.

Some of them said: What is meant by that is that it is not too narrow for you to stay in a place on it where it is not permissible for you to stay, but if there is a practice in a place on it that involves disobedience to God and you are not able to change it, then flee from it.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement, Indeed, My earth is spacious, he said: If someone commits sins in it, then leave it.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr,
m: regarding his statement, Indeed, My earth is spacious, he said: If someone commits sins in it, then leave it.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: Flee, for my land is vast.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ata’, who said:
m: If you are commanded to commit sins, then flee, for My earth is vast.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sharik told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ata’,
m: My earth is spacious. He said: Avoiding the people of sin.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, Indeed, My earth is spacious, so they migrated and fought.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
O My servants who have believed
, indeed My earth is spacious,
h
so worship Me
. I said: Does He mean by this those believers who were in Mecca? He said: Yes.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: What I have brought forth from my land for you in terms of provision is abundant for you.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Zaid bin Al-Habbab told me, on the authority of Shaddad bin Saeed bin Malik Abi Talha Al-Rasibi, on the authority of Ghailan bin Jarir Al-Ma’wali, on the authority of Mutraf bin Abdullah bin Al-Shakheer Al-Amiri,
m: regarding the statement of God, Indeed, My earth is spacious, he said: Indeed, My provision for you is spacious.
b.via: Mutraf bin Abdullah bin Al-Shakheer Al-Amiri

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: Zaid bin Habbab told us, on the authority of Shaddad, on the authority of Ghailan bin Jarir, on the authority of Mutraf bin Al-Shaikher,
m: My land is vast, meaning: My provision for you is vast. The first of the two interpretations of the verse is the statement of those who said: The meaning of this is: My earth is vast, so flee from those who prevent you from working in obedience to Me, because His statement,
h
Then worship Me indicates

that, and that this is the more apparent of its two meanings, and that is because when He describes the earth with a description, then the most common way of describing it with that is that it is not all too narrow for someone who finds a place in it too narrow, not that He described it with an abundance of goodness and fertility. His saying,
h
So worship Me
, means: So devote your worship and obedience to Me, and do not obey anyone in disobeying Me.

x: God Almighty says to the believers in Him from the companions of His Prophet: Migrate from the land of polytheism, Mecca, to the land of Islam, Medina, for My land is vast, so be patient in worshipping Me, and be sincere in obeying Me, for you will die and will return to Me, because every living soul will taste death, and then after death you will return to Us. Then He, the Most High, informed them of what He has prepared for those among them who are patient in obeying Him, of His honor with Him.
