He said: And those who believed, meaning, believed in God and His Messenger, in what he brought from God, and did righteous deeds, meaning, and did what God commanded them to do and obeyed Him in it, and refrained from what He forbade them from, We will surely assign them lofty chambers in Paradise, meaning, We will surely place them in the highest levels of Paradise. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufians recited it as lanbaw’inhum with the letter ba and the majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it with the letter tha lanthwaynahum. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings among the reciters of the regions. One of them has been recited by scholars among the reciters, and they are close in meaning. So whichever of them the reciter recites, he is correct.

This is because his saying we will settle them is from I will settle him down meaning I will bring him down. Likewise, we will bring them down is from I will bring him down meaning I will bring him down and likewise we will bring them down is from I will bring him down meaning I will bring him down from I will bring him down which is the place to stay. And His statement, Underneath it rivers flow, means: rivers flow beneath its trees. Abiding therein, means: remaining therein forever. Excellent is the reward of those who work, means: excellent is the reward of those who work in obedience to God. These are the rooms in which God will house them in His gardens, beneath which rivers flow.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of this.

The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufians recited it as lanbaw’inhum with the letter ba and the majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it with the letter tha lanthwaynahum.
The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings among the reciters of the regions.
One of them has been recited by scholars among the reciters, and they are close in meaning.

x: Those who were patient in the face of the harm of the polytheists in this world, and what they were subjected to from them, and in working in obedience to God and what pleases Him, and in jihad against His enemies, and upon their Lord they rely in their provisions and jihad against their enemies, so they do not turn back from them, trusting that God will make His word supreme, and weaken the plot of the disbelievers, and that whatever provision He has allotted them will not escape them.

God Almighty says to the believers in Him and His Messenger from the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Emigrate and strive in the cause of God, O believers, against His enemies, and do not fear poverty or scarcity. How many creatures are in need of food, drink, and provision, but they do not carry their provisions, meaning they do not carry their provisions, so they carry them from one day to the next because they are unable to do so. “God provides for them and for you” day by day. And He is the All-Hearing of your words. We fear poverty because of our separation from our homelands. The All-Knowing of what is in your souls, and what your affair will come to, and the affair of your enemy from God’s humiliation of them, and your victory over them, and other than that of your affairs. Nothing of the affairs of His creation is hidden from Him. And in a similar manner to what we said in interpreting that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And how many a creature does not carry its own provision
? He said: Birds and animals do not carry provisions.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us:
m: I heard Imran, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, regarding this verse, And how many a creature carries not its own provision? God provides for it and for you. He said: There are creatures that cannot store up provision for tomorrow, but are provided with provision every day until they die.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ali bin Al-Aqmar:
m: h
And how many a creature does not carry its own provision
. He said: It does not store anything for tomorrow.

x: God Almighty says: And if you ask, O Muhammad, these polytheists who created the heavens and the earth and proportioned them, and subjected the sun and the moon to His servants, running constantly for the benefit of God’s creation, they will surely say, The One who created that and did it is God. “How then are they deluded?” God Almighty says: How can they be turned away from the One who did that, and turn away from sincerely worshipping Him?

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: How can they be deceived? meaning, they are just.

x: God Almighty says: God expands His provision for whomever He wills of His creation, and restricts and is stingy for whomever He wills of them. He says: Your provisions and their distribution among you, O people, are in My hand, not mine, for anyone else. I expand from them to whomever I will, and I restrict them to whomever I will. So do not let fear of poverty prevent you from emigrating and fighting your enemy. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things. He says that God is Knowing of your interests, and of those for whom nothing is right except abundance in provision, and of those for whom nothing is right except stinginess, and He is All-Knowing of that.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And if you ask, O Muhammad, these polytheists among your people, Who sent down water from the sky? - which is the rain that God sends down from the clouds - and revived the earth thereby. He says: He revived the earth with the water that came down from the sky, and reviving it: causing plants to grow in it after its death, after its drought and barrenness. His statement, They will surely say, ‘God,’ means: They will say, ‘The One who did that is God, to Whom all things are entitled to worship.’ His statement, Say, ‘Praise be to God,’ means: And if they say that, and he says, Praise be to God, “But most of them do not reason,” means: Rather, most of these polytheists do not reason about what is beneficial to them in their religion and what is harmful to them. So, due to their ignorance, they think that by worshipping deities other than God, they will attain closeness and nearness to God. They do not know that they are doomed and deserving of eternal damnation in the Fire.

God Almighty says: And this worldly life which these polytheists enjoy is nothing but amusement and play meaning, nothing but the souls’ enjoyment of what they enjoy, then it will soon end, with no permanence or permanence. And indeed, the home of the Hereafter - that is the life meaning, And indeed, in the home of the Hereafter is the eternal life that does not end, cease, or die with it.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, And indeed, the home of the Hereafter - that is the life, if they only knew is life in which there is no death.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
It is the life
, he said: There is no death in it.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, And indeed, the home of the Hereafter - that is the life, he said: It is eternal. His saying, If they had known, means: If these polytheists had known that this was the case, they would have refrained from denying God and associating others with Him in His worship, but they do not know that.

x: God Almighty says: So when these polytheists boarded a ship at sea, and feared drowning and perishing in it, they called upon God, devoting their religion to Him sincerely. He says: They devoted their monotheism to God when the hardship befell them, and devoted obedience to Him alone, and submitted to Him in worship, and did not seek help from their gods and rivals, but from God who created them. Then when He delivered them to the land. He says: When He delivered them from what they were in and made them safe, and they reached the land, they made a partner with God in their worship, and they called upon the gods and idols with Him as lords.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, But when He delivered them to the land, at once they associated others with Him, so all of creation acknowledges that God is their Lord, then they associate others with Him after that.

x: God Almighty says: So when God saved these polytheists from the fear and caution they were in at sea, and from drowning to the shore, when they reached the shore, they associated with God other gods and rivals, to disbelieve in what We have given them. That is, to deny the blessing of God that He bestowed upon them in themselves and their wealth.
h
And that they may enjoy
themselves. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it as Waytamattu with a kasra on the lam, meaning:
h
And that they may enjoy

themselves, We gave them that. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as Waytamattu with a sukoon on the lam, as a threat and a rebuke: meaning, disbelieve, for you will soon learn what they will encounter of God's punishment for their disbelief in Him. And the first of the two readings of that, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who read it with a sukoon on the lam as a threat and warning.
That is because those who read it with a kasra on the lam claimed that they chose to break it in conjunction with the lam in His statement:
h
So that they may disbelieve
, and that His statement
h
So that they may disbelieve since its meaning
was:
h
So that they may disbelieve
, the correct thing in His statement
h
And that they may enjoy
was:
h
And that they may enjoy
, since it was in conjunction with His statement:
h
So that they may disbelieve
, according to them. And what they went with that is not a school of thought, and that is because the lam of His statement
h
So that they may disbelieve could be in the meaning of So that they may enjoy
, because it is a condition for His statement:
h
If they associate partners with God so that they may disbelieve in what We have given them of blessings
, and that is not the case with His statement
h
And that they may enjoy

, because their association with God was disbelief in His blessings, and their association with Him was not enjoyment of the world, even if association with Him facilitates for them the path to enjoyment of it.

So since that is the case, then directing it to the meaning of a threat is more appropriate and more worthy than directing it to the meaning of: So that they may enjoy. And then he mentioned that in Abu’s reading it is and enjoy, and this is evidence of the correctness of the one who read it with a silent lam meaning threat.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of this.
The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it as Waytamattu with a kasra on the lam, meaning: And that they may enjoy themselves, We gave them that.

The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as Waytamattu with a sukoon on the lam, as a threat and a rebuke: meaning, disbelieve, for you will soon learn what they will encounter of God's punishment for their disbelief in Him.
And the first of the two readings of that, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who read it with a sukoon on the lam as a threat and warning.

That is because those who read it with a kasra on the lam claimed that they chose to break it in conjunction with the lam in His statement: So that they may disbelieve, and that His statement So that they may disbelieve since its meaning was: So that they may disbelieve, the correct thing in His statement And that they may enjoy was: And that they may enjoy, since it was in conjunction with His statement: So that they may disbelieve, according to them.
And then he mentioned that in Abu’s reading it is and enjoy, and this is evidence of the correctness of the one who read it with a silent lam meaning threat.

x: And His statement,
h
Have they not seen that We have made a secure sanctuary

? God Almighty says, reminding these polytheists from Quraysh, who say: Why was a sign not sent down to him from his Lord, His favor upon them with which He singled them out from among all other people, despite their disbelief in His favor and their associating other gods and rivals with Him in His worship: Have these polytheists from Quraysh not seen that We singled them out from among Our favors upon them, to the exclusion of all other servants, so that they may thank Us for that and refrain from their disbelief in Us and their associating in Our cloak that which neither benefits Us nor harms them? We have made their land a sanctuary, forbidding people to enter it by raid or war, safe, in which whoever lives there is safe, so he takes refuge in it from captivity, fear, and the forbidden which no one else among people feels safe from.
And people are snatched away from around them. He says: And people are taken away from around them by killing and captivity.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Have they not seen that We have made a secure sanctuary while people are being snatched away all around them
? He said: There was a sign for them in that that people are being attacked and snatched away while they are safe. And his statement,
h
Do they then believe in falsehood

? He says: Do they then acknowledge the divinity of idols by associating partners with God, and deny the blessing of God with which He has made their country a safe sanctuary? He means by his statement, Do they then disbelieve? They deny.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
Then do they believe in falsehood
?: meaning in polytheism, and disbelieve in the favor of God?: meaning they deny.

x: God the Almighty says: “And who is more unjust, O people, than he who invents a lie against God and says, when they commit an immorality, ‘We found our fathers doing it, and God has commanded us to do it.’ And God does not command immorality.” Or he denied the truth when it came to him. He says: Or he denied what God sent His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with of His Oneness and disavowal of deities and rivals when this truth came to him from God. Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers? He says: Is there not in Hell an abode and dwelling for he who disbelieves in God, denies His Oneness and denies His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace? This is a statement, not a question. Rather, it is the statement of Jarir: Aren't you the best of those who ride mounts and the most generous of the worlds in terms of their bellies?

c: He only informed us that
m: the unbelievers in God have a place of abode in Hell, and a home in which they will abide.

x: God Almighty says: And those who fought these infidels of Quraysh who falsely attributed falsehood to God, who denied the truth when it came to them concerning Us, seeking through their fighting to make Our word supreme and to support Our religion, We will surely guide them to Our ways meaning: We will surely guide them to the straight paths, and that is to follow the religion of God, which is Islam, with which God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And indeed, God is with the doers of good meaning: And indeed, God is with whoever does good among His creation, who strives against the polytheists in it, believing in what His Messenger brought from God with aid for him and victory over whoever strives against his enemies. And in a similar manner to what we said in the interpretation of His statement,
h
And those who strive for Us
, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And those who strive for Us
, so I said to him: Did they fight for Us? He said: Yes.

notes.en: Ibn Saʿd transmitted it in al-Ṭabaqāt (6/262) through al-Aʿmash. Ibn Abī Ḥātim in his Tafsīr (9/3075) and al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-īmān (no. 7187) transmitted it through al-Aʿmash, from Rabīʿ ibn Abī Rāshid, from Saʿīd, adding Rabīʿ to the chain. Through Rabīʿ, ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr (2/99), as did Ibn Abī Shaybah (13/540); through Ibn Abī Shaybah, Abū Nuʿaym transmitted it in Ḥilyat al-awliyāʾ (4/284). Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr (5/149) to al-Firyābī.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن سعد في الطبقات 6/ 262 من طريق الأعمش به. وأخرجه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره 9/ 3075، والبيهقي في الشعب (7187) من طريق الأعمش عن ربيع بن أبي راشد عن سعيد به، فزاد ربيعًا في سنده، ومن طريق ربيع هذا أخرجه عبد الرزاق فى تفسيره 2/ 99، وابن أبي شيبة 13/ 540، ومن طريقه أبو نعيم في الحلية 4/ 284، وعزاه السيوطى فى الدر المنثور 5/ 149 إلى الفريابي.
